                    if abs(dbp_secs[j] - target) <= tol:
                        tt = t_sbp_w[i]
                        map_val = _map_from_bp(sbp_w[i], dbp_w[j])
                        pairs_t.append(tt)
                        pairs_map.append(map_val)

                # DBP->SBP nearest
                for j in range(t_dbp_w.size):
                    target = dbp_secs[j]
                    i = int(np.argmin(np.abs(sbp_secs - target)))
                    if abs(sbp_secs[i] - target) <= tol:
                        tt = t_dbp_w[j]
                        map_val = _map_from_bp(sbp_w[i], dbp_w[j])
                        pairs_t.append(tt)
                        pairs_map.append(map_val)

                if len(pairs_t) > 0:
                    # Deduplicate by timestamp (keep mean if duplicates)
                    # Convert times to integer seconds since epoch for grouping
                    epoch_secs = np.array([int((tt - np.datetime64('1970-01-01T00:00:00')).astype('timedelta64[s]').astype(int)) for tt in np.array(pairs_t, dtype=object)], dtype=int)
                    order = np.argsort(epoch_secs)
                    epoch_secs = epoch_secs[order]
                    pairs_map_arr = np.array(pairs_map, dtype=float)[order]

                    uniq_secs, idx_start = np.unique(epoch_secs, return_index=True)
                    map_uniq = np.empty(uniq_secs.shape[0], dtype=float)
                    for k in range(uniq_secs.shape[0]):
                        start = idx_start[k]
                        end = idx_start[k + 1] if k + 1 < idx_start.size else epoch_secs.size
                        map_uniq[k] = float(np.nanmean(pairs_map_arr[start:end]))
                    # Convert back to datetimes anchored to epoch
                    pairs_map = map_uniq
                    pairs_t = np.array([np.datetime64('1970-01-01T00:00:00') + np.timedelta64(int(s), 's') for s in uniq_secs], dtype=object)
                else:
                    pairs_map = np.array([], dtype=float)
                    pairs_t = np.array([], dtype=object)
            else:
                pairs_map = np.array([], dtype=float)
                pairs_t = np.array([], dtype=object)

            # Align HR to MAP by nearest HR sample for each MAP timestamp within 2 minutes
            if len(pairs_map) > 0 and t_hr.size > 0:
                hr_secs_full = np.array([(tt - t0).astype('timedelta64[s]').astype(int) for tt in t_hr[(t_hr >= t0) & (t_hr <= t1)]], dtype=int)
                hr_vals_full = v_hr[(t_hr >= t0) & (t_hr <= t1)]
                map_secs = np.array([(tt - t0).astype('timedelta64[s]').astype(int) for tt in np.array(pairs_t, dtype=object)], dtype=int)

                hr_aligned = []
                map_aligned = []
                if hr_secs_full.size > 0:
                    for msec, mval in zip(map_secs, np.asarray(pairs_map, dtype=float)):
                        i = int(np.argmin(np.abs(hr_secs_full - msec)))
                        if abs(hr_secs_full[i] - msec) <= 120:
                            hr_aligned.append(float(hr_vals_full[i]))
                            map_aligned.append(float(mval))
                hr_aligned = np.array(hr_aligned, dtype=float)
                map_aligned = np.array(map_aligned, dtype=float)
            else:
                hr_aligned = np.array([], dtype=float)
                map_aligned = np.array([], dtype=float)

            n_pairs = int(min(hr_aligned.size, map_aligned.size))
            if n_pairs >= min_pairs:
                r, p = _pearsonr_safe(hr_aligned, map_aligned)
            else:
                r, p = np.nan, np.nan

            ct = _window_center_time(t0, t1)
            corr_times.append(ct)
            corr_r.append(r)
            corr_p.append(p)
            n_pairs_list.append(n_pairs)

            if np.isfinite(r) and r < inverse_threshold:
                flagged.append({
                    "start": t0,
                    "end": t1,
                    "center_time": ct,
                    "r": float(r),
                    "p_value": float(p) if np.isfinite(p) else np.nan,
                    "n_pairs": n_pairs
                })

        # Prepare plot
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(10, 4))
        ax.plot(corr_times, corr_r, color="black", linewidth=1.5, label="Rolling Pearson r (HR vs MAP)")
        ax.axhline(0.0, color="gray", linewidth=1.0)
        ax.axhline(inverse_threshold, color="red", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2, label=f"Inverse threshold r<{inverse_threshold}")

        # Shade flagged intervals
        for f in flagged:
            ax.axvspan(f["start"], f["end"], color="red", alpha=0.12)

        ax.set_title(f"Rolling HR–MAP Pearson Correlation (window={window_minutes:.0f} min, step={step_minutes:.0f} min)")
        ax.set_ylabel("Pearson r")
        ax.set_xlabel("Time")
        ax.set_ylim(-1.05, 1.05)
        ax.legend(loc="lower right", frameon=True)

        # Annotate with current shock markers (from state) for context
        ax.text(0.01, 0.02,
                f"Shock Index={shock_index:.3f} ({shock_index_interpretation.split('.')[0]}) | MAP={map_value:.0f} mmHg ({map_interpretation.split('.')[0]})",
                transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=9, va="bottom", ha="left")

        save_plot("rolling_hr_map_correlation.png", fig=fig)

        # Assemble result
        corr_series = []
        for ct, r, p, npairs in zip(corr_times, corr_r, corr_p, n_pairs_list):
            corr_series.append({
                "center_time": ct,
                "r": float(r) if np.isfinite(r) else np.nan,
                "p_value": float(p) if np.isfinite(p) else np.nan,
                "n_pairs": int(npairs)
            })

        valid_rs = np.array([x for x in corr_r if np.isfinite(x)], dtype=float)
        if valid_rs.size > 0:
            r_min = float(np.min(valid_rs))
            r_med = float(np.median(valid_rs))
        else:
            r_min = np.nan
            r_med = np.nan

        result = {
            "window_minutes": float(window_minutes),
            "step_minutes": float(step_minutes),
            "min_pairs": int(min_pairs),
            "inverse_threshold": float(inverse_threshold),
            "n_windows": int(len(corr_times)),
            "n_windows_valid": int(valid_rs.size),
            "r_min": r_min,
            "r_median": r_med,
            "n_flagged": int(len(flagged)),
            "flagged_intervals": flagged,
            "correlation_series": corr_series,
            "plot_file": "rolling_hr_map_correlation.png"
        }

        if valid_rs.size == 0:
            interpretation = "Rolling HR–MAP correlation could not be computed due to insufficient paired HR and BP data within windows."
        else:
            if len(flagged) > 0:
                interpretation = f"Rolling HR–MAP correlation shows {len(flagged)}/{len(corr_times)} intervals with strong inverse coupling (r<{inverse_threshold}), which can indicate hemodynamic decompensation (tachycardia with falling MAP) in this high-risk patient."
            else:
                interpretation = f"Rolling HR–MAP correlation does not show strong inverse coupling (no windows with r<{inverse_threshold}); however, global perfusion remains concerning given MAP {map_value:.0f} mmHg and shock index {shock_index:.2f}."

Working diagnosis at Iteration 0: **Fall likely related to hypotension/volume depletion or delirium**, with **high-risk occult injury** (intracranial bleed/occult fracture) and **need to rule out infection/aspiration recurrence** given history and qSOFA flagged as high risk in the provided metrics.

- **Mental status/GCS and baseline comparison** (qSOFA includes AMS; we need actual exam: orientation, focal deficits, delirium features).

- **Timing/temporal alignment of vitals** (are hypotensive episodes concurrent with tachycardia, desaturation, or tachypnea? single transient values vs sustained).
- **Oxygen delivery context** (room air vs supplemental O2; waveform/pleth quality when SpO2 hit 81%).
- **Pain/injury exam findings** (hip pain, inability to bear weight, chest wall pain; signs of dehydration; GI bleed signs; urinary retention/infection symptoms).
- **Repeat/confirmatory BP method** (cuff size, manual confirmation, positional readings) given SBP nadir 75.
- **Respiratory exam context** (cough, witnessed aspiration, new sputum, increased work of breathing) since RR range includes up to 26.6.

# Hypotheses
1. **Orthostatic hypotension / dehydration** causing fall (supported by SBP mean ~92, nadir 75; elevated shock index 0.94).
2. **Occult infection with atypical presentation** (urosepsis/aspiration pneumonia) causing weakness/delirium and relative hypotension (history of septic shock; low-normal temps do not exclude).
3. **Aspiration event or evolving pneumonitis/pneumonia** (prior aspiration pneumonitis; SpO2 low outlier 81%—needs validation).
4. **Intracranial hemorrhage or concussion** after fall (high-risk age; need head strike/anticoagulation/AMS details).
5. **Occult fracture (hip/pelvis/ribs/vertebral)** contributing to pain, immobility, and physiologic stress (pain can drive HR ~110).
6. **Cardiac dysrhythmia / cardiogenic syncope** (no rhythm data provided; tachycardia range modest but fall mechanism unknown).
7. **Medication/toxin effect** (even if “no recorded meds,” elderly often have antihypertensives/sedatives contributing to hypotension/falls).

    if np.nanstd(x) == 0 or np.nanstd(y) == 0:

    m = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)

            corr_times.append(ct)
            corr_r.append(r)
            corr_p.append(p)
            n_pairs_list.append(n_pairs)

            if np.isfinite(r) and r < inverse_threshold:
                flagged.append({
                    "start": t0,
                    "end": t1,
                    "center_time": ct,
                    "r": float(r),
                    "p_value": float(p) if np.isfinite(p) else np.nan,
                    "n_pairs": n_pairs
                })

        # Plot
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(10, 4))
        ax.plot(corr_times, corr_r, color="black", linewidth=1.5, label="Rolling Pearson r (HR vs MAP)")
        ax.axhline(0.0, color="gray", linewidth=1.0)
        ax.axhline(inverse_threshold, color="red", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2, label=f"Inverse threshold r<{inverse_threshold}")

        for f in flagged:
            ax.axvspan(f["start"], f["end"], color="red", alpha=0.12)

        ax.set_title(f"Rolling HR–MAP Pearson Correlation (window={window_minutes:.0f} min, step={step_minutes:.0f} min)")
        ax.set_ylabel("Pearson r")
        ax.set_xlabel("Time")
        ax.set_ylim(-1.05, 1.05)
        ax.legend(loc="lower right", frameon=True)

        ax.text(
            0.01, 0.02,
            f"Shock Index={shock_index:.3f} ({shock_index_interpretation.split('.')[0]}) | MAP={map_value:.0f} mmHg ({map_interpretation.split('.')[0]})",
            transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=9, va="bottom", ha="left"
        )

        save_plot("rolling_hr_map_correlation.png", fig=fig)

        corr_series = []
        for ct, r, p, npairs in zip(corr_times, corr_r, corr_p, n_pairs_list):
            corr_series.append({
                "center_time": ct,
                "r": float(r) if np.isfinite(r) else np.nan,
                "p_value": float(p) if np.isfinite(p) else np.nan,
                "n_pairs": int(npairs)
            })

        valid_rs = np.array([x for x in corr_r if np.isfinite(x)], dtype=float)
        r_min = float(np.min(valid_rs)) if valid_rs.size > 0 else np.nan
        r_med = float(np.median(valid_rs)) if valid_rs.size > 0 else np.nan

        result = {
            "window_minutes": float(window_minutes),
            "step_minutes": float(step_minutes),
            "min_pairs": int(min_pairs),
            "inverse_threshold": float(inverse_threshold),
            "pair_tol_seconds": float(pair_tol_seconds),
            "n_windows": int(len(corr_times)),
            "n_windows_valid": int(valid_rs.size),
            "r_min": r_min,
            "r_median": r_med,
            "n_flagged": int(len(flagged)),
            "flagged_intervals": flagged,
            "correlation_series": corr_series,
            "plot_file": "rolling_hr_map_correlation.png"
        }

        if valid_rs.size == 0:
            interpretation = "Rolling HR–MAP correlation could not be computed due to insufficient paired HR and BP data within windows."
        else:
            if len(flagged) > 0:
                interpretation = f"Rolling HR–MAP correlation shows {len(flagged)}/{len(corr_times)} intervals with strong inverse coupling (r<{inverse_threshold}), consistent with periods of tachycardia accompanying falling perfusion pressure (MAP)."
            else:
                interpretation = f"Rolling HR–MAP correlation does not show strong inverse coupling (no windows with r<{inverse_threshold}); despite this, absolute perfusion remains low (MAP {map_value:.0f} mmHg) with elevated shock index ({shock_index:.2f})."

Current vitals profile shows **persistent tachycardia** (HR mean **104**, range **88.5–121.6**) and **tachypnea** (RR mean **25.4**, range **14.5–37.4**) with generally preserved oxygenation (SpO2 mean **98.9%**) but **documented severe desaturation to 75.9%**. Overall, the vital-sign pattern plus acute neuro complaint suggests a **high-risk, potentially time-sensitive** condition: (1) **CNS catastrophe** (ischemic stroke/ICH) with secondary autonomic instability/aspiration, and/or (2) **sepsis with encephalopathy** or other shock state (e.g., occult hemorrhage, cardiogenic/arrhythmic, dehydration) manifesting as AMS.

**Key missing data (clinically critical):**
- The **timeline** of vital derangements: when did SBP 51 occur; was it transient vs sustained; relation to desaturation events.
- **Mental status details**: last known well, focal deficits, GCS, delirium vs coma, seizures.
- **Respiratory context**: oxygen delivery method during SpO2 75.9 (room air vs supplemental), waveform quality, aspiration risk.
- **Hemodynamic context**: orthostasis, signs of bleeding, fluid status; whether hypotension coincides with tachycardia surges.
- **No labs available** limits confirmation of infection/ischemia/metabolic causes; we must lean on vitals trends and clinical neuro findings.

1. **Acute ischemic stroke / TIA** with secondary aspiration risk and stress tachycardia; must consider large-vessel occlusion given age and instability (neuro complaint drives this high on list).
2. **Intracerebral hemorrhage / SAH** (especially with SBP spikes up to **186**) causing acute AMS; hypotension episodes could represent evolving shock from another source or measurement/artifact, but SBP **51** is too low to ignore.
3. **Sepsis with sepsis-associated encephalopathy** (qSOFA **2**, persistent HR/RR elevation); afebrile elderly sepsis remains plausible despite T ~**36.5°C**.
4. **Aspiration pneumonitis/pneumonia** causing episodic severe hypoxemia (**SpO2 75.9%**) and tachypnea.
5. **Cardiogenic/arrhythmic event** (persistent tachycardia, hypotension episodes) leading to cerebral hypoperfusion/AMS.

## Objective
1. **Identify Clinical Gaps**: Find confirmation bias, missed rule-outs, or life-threats ignored by the Doctor's working diagnosis and plan.
2. **Visual Evidence Is Required**: Do not just suggest a rule-out. Explicitly request plots or images to support your critique. These visuals provide the objective evidence needed to justify a change in clinical direction.

You must output your response in the following Markdown format. Do not use JSON.

[Sharp clinical critique of the Doctor's plan. Highlight confirmation bias, missed 'Can't Miss' life-threats, or missing rule-outs.]

# Differential Diagnosis
[List of alternative diagnoses that MUST be considered.]
- [Diagnosis 1]
- [Diagnosis 2]

[Specific metrics or plots to rule out the alternative diagnoses.]
- [Task 1]
- [Task 2]

# Critique
Your current frame leans heavily toward **hypovolemia/orthostasis vs occult infection**, which is reasonable given recurrent low SBP + SI ~1–1.4 and narrow PP. The main gap is that the **pattern could also be driven by intermittent dysrhythmia/low stroke volume states** that *mimic* “dehydration physiology” on spot BPs—especially in an 85M with frailty and prior shock.

Two high-risk pitfalls to avoid:

1) **Occult cardiogenic/obstructive physiology hiding inside “narrow pulse pressure + high SI.”**  
Narrow PP is not specific for hypovolemia; it’s also a classic signal for **low stroke volume** (LV dysfunction, critical AS, tamponade physiology, PE with RV compromise). Without labs/imaging, the only way we can pressure-test this with available data is to look for **coupling/decoupling** between SBP, DBP, and HR over time (e.g., falling SBP with *rising* DBP → ↑SVR compensation; or falling SBP with *falling* DBP → vasodilatory pattern). Your current visuals show SI/PP but not whether the **diastolic behavior supports vasodilation vs pump failure**.

2) **The SpO2 “artifact” conclusion may be too confident without pleth context—so use *time-domain structure* of SpO2 rather than only episode rules.**  
Single-point desats can still represent true transient events (brief aspiration, apneic spells, atelectasis, positional hypoventilation), and in older patients even brief hypoxemia can precipitate **arrhythmia/syncope/fall**. The current definition (≥2 consecutive readings) can miss true events if sampling is sparse or if the monitor drops only one value. You already did episode plots; what’s missing is a **quality check using temporal clustering and cross-signal concordance** (HR/RR changes around the desat). If those “outliers” coincide with RR changes or HR surges, they’re less likely artifact.

Also: your temperature interpretation is good, but the dataset is internally inconsistent (mean 36.70 with a max 36.8 and min 35.2 suggests rounding/site switching). A *relative rise* strategy needs **trajectory** rather than single cutoffs.

# Differential Diagnosis
- **Intermittent dysrhythmia / tachy-brady syndrome** causing syncope/fall with secondary hypotension (not excluded by spot HR range 80–110 if events are brief or missed).
- **Low-stroke-volume state** (LV dysfunction, critical aortic stenosis, RV strain/PE, or less likely tamponade physiology) presenting as narrow PP + elevated SI.

# Rule-out Tasks
- **Hemodynamic pattern classification plot (vasodilatory vs low-SV signature):**  
  Create a time-aligned plot of **SBP, DBP, and derived PP**, and add a **scatter/phase plot of (SBP vs DBP)** with points colored by **HR quartile**. Also compute/plot a rolling correlation (e.g., 10–15 min rolling Spearman) between **SBP↔DBP** and **PP↔HR**.  
  *Why this helps:*  
  - **Vasodilatory physiology** tends to show **lower DBP** and SBP/DBP falling together, with PP not necessarily extremely low.  
  - **Low stroke volume/pump states** often show **disproportionately narrow PP** and compensatory **higher DBP/↑SVR** (or SBP falling with relatively preserved DBP), plus tighter PP–HR coupling.

- **SpO2 outlier validation via concordance/cluster analysis (artifact vs true transient event):**  
  For each SpO2 value <90% (even singletons), generate a ±10 minute aligned panel showing **SpO2, HR, RR**, and compute a small table of **ΔHR and ΔRR** from baseline (e.g., median of prior 5 min) to nadir. Additionally, plot the **inter-reading interval distribution** around those points (to detect gaps/monitor dropouts) and a **rolling median + rolling MAD** of SpO2 to detect true transient dips versus isolated telemetry glitches.  
  *Why this helps:* true physiologic desaturation usually has **signal concordance** (RR/HR response or at least temporal clustering), whereas pure artifact often has **timing gaps/isolated spikes** without accompanying cardiorespiratory response.

These two add-ons stay strictly within available signals and directly challenge the two “can’t miss” alternatives (arrhythmic/cardiogenic vs artifact-mislabeled transient hypoxemia) without duplicating your existing vitals panels or SI/PP plots.

# Rolling-window Pearson correlation between HR and MAP (computed from SBP/DBP within window)
# Outputs: result (dict) and interpretation (str); also saves plot.

def _to_arrays(ts_list):
    if ts_list is None or len(ts_list) == 0:
        return np.array([]), np.array([])
    t = np.array([x[0] for x in ts_list], dtype=object)
    v = np.array([float(x[1]) for x in ts_list], dtype=float)
    return t, v

def _map_from_bp(sbps, dbps):
    return (sbps + 2.0 * dbps) / 3.0

def _window_center_time(t_start, t_end):
    # Return midpoint datetime
    return t_start + (t_end - t_start) / 2

def _pearsonr_safe(x, y):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    if x.size < 3 or y.size < 3:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    if np.nanstd(x) == 0 or np.nanstd(y) == 0:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    m = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    if m.sum() < 3:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    r, p = stats.pearsonr(x[m], y[m])
    return float(r), float(p)

# Parameters
window_minutes = 12.0  # within requested 10–15 min
step_minutes = 2.0
min_pairs = 5
inverse_threshold = -0.5

# Extract series
t_hr, v_hr = _to_arrays(heart_rate)
t_sbp, v_sbp = _to_arrays(systolic_bp)
t_dbp, v_dbp = _to_arrays(diastolic_bp)

# Determine analysis interval based on available data
all_times = []
if t_hr.size > 0: all_times.append(t_hr[0]); all_times.append(t_hr[-1])
if t_sbp.size > 0: all_times.append(t_sbp[0]); all_times.append(t_sbp[-1])
if t_dbp.size > 0: all_times.append(t_dbp[0]); all_times.append(t_dbp[-1])

if len(all_times) == 0:
    result = {
        "window_minutes": window_minutes,
        "step_minutes": step_minutes,
        "min_pairs": min_pairs,
        "inverse_threshold": inverse_threshold,
        "n_windows": 0,
        "n_flagged": 0,
        "flagged_intervals": [],
        "correlation_series": []
    }
    interpretation = "Insufficient data to compute rolling HR–MAP correlation."
else:
    t_min = min(all_times)
    t_max = max(all_times)
    if (t_max - t_min).total_seconds() / 60.0 < window_minutes:
        # Not enough time span for at least one full window
        result = {
            "window_minutes": window_minutes,
            "step_minutes": step_minutes,
            "min_pairs": min_pairs,
            "inverse_threshold": inverse_threshold,
            "n_windows": 0,
            "n_flagged": 0,
            "flagged_intervals": [],
            "correlation_series": []
        }
        interpretation = "Time span is shorter than rolling window; cannot compute HR–MAP correlation."
    else:
        # Create window start times
        step_seconds = step_minutes * 60.0
        win_seconds = window_minutes * 60.0

        # Use numpy to build datetime list safely
        n_steps = int(np.floor(((t_max - t_min).total_seconds() - win_seconds) / step_seconds)) + 1
        window_starts = [t_min + np.timedelta64(int(i * step_seconds), 's') for i in range(max(n_steps, 0))]

        # Helper to slice within (start, end]
        def _slice_between(t_arr, v_arr, t0, t1):
            if t_arr.size == 0:
                return np.array([]), np.array([])
            m = (t_arr >= t0) & (t_arr <= t1)
            return t_arr[m], v_arr[m]

        corr_times = []
        corr_r = []
        corr_p = []
        n_pairs_list = []
        flagged = []

        for t0 in window_starts:
            t1 = t0 + np.timedelta64(int(win_seconds), 's')

            # Slice HR
            _, hr_w = _slice_between(t_hr, v_hr, t0, t1)

            # Slice BP and compute MAP (pair SBP/DBP within window by nearest-neighbor merge on timestamps)
            t_sbp_w, sbp_w = _slice_between(t_sbp, v_sbp, t0, t1)
            t_dbp_w, dbp_w = _slice_between(t_dbp, v_dbp, t0, t1)

            # Build MAP samples by timestamp alignment:
            # Strategy: for each SBP timestamp, find nearest DBP timestamp in window within 2 minutes; similarly for DBP->SBP
            # Then create unique paired timestamps to reduce bias.
            pairs_t = []
            pairs_map = []

            if t_sbp_w.size > 0 and t_dbp_w.size > 0:
                # Precompute DBP times in seconds relative to window start for fast nearest search
                dbp_secs = np.array([(tt - t0).astype('timedelta64[s]').astype(int) for tt in t_dbp_w], dtype=int)
                sbp_secs = np.array([(tt - t0).astype('timedelta64[s]').astype(int) for tt in t_sbp_w], dtype=int)

                # Tolerance: 120 seconds
                tol = 120

                # SBP->DBP nearest
                for i in range(t_sbp_w.size):
                    target = sbp_secs[i]
                    j = int(np.argmin(np.abs(dbp_secs - target)))
                    if abs(dbp_secs[j] - target) <= tol:
                        tt = t_sbp_w[i]
                        map_val = _map_from_bp(sbp_w[i], dbp_w[j])
                        pairs_t.append(tt)
                        pairs_map.append(map_val)

                # DBP->SBP nearest
                for j in range(t_dbp_w.size):
                    target = dbp_secs[j]
                    i = int(np.argmin(np.abs(sbp_secs - target)))
                    if abs(sbp_secs[i] - target) <= tol:
                        tt = t_dbp_w[j]
                        map_val = _map_from_bp(sbp_w[i], dbp_w[j])
                        pairs_t.append(tt)
                        pairs_map.append(map_val)

                if len(pairs_t) > 0:
                    # Deduplicate by timestamp (keep mean if duplicates)
                    # Convert times to integer seconds since epoch for grouping
                    epoch_secs = np.array([int((tt - np.datetime64('1970-01-01T00:00:00')).astype('timedelta64[s]').astype(int)) for tt in np.array(pairs_t, dtype=object)], dtype=int)
                    order = np.argsort(epoch_secs)
                    epoch_secs = epoch_secs[order]
                    pairs_map_arr = np.array(pairs_map, dtype=float)[order]

                    uniq_secs, idx_start = np.unique(epoch_secs, return_index=True)
                    map_uniq = np.empty(uniq_secs.shape[0], dtype=float)
                    for k in range(uniq_secs.shape[0]):
                        start = idx_start[k]
                        end = idx_start[k + 1] if k + 1 < idx_start.size else epoch_secs.size
                        map_uniq[k] = float(np.nanmean(pairs_map_arr[start:end]))
                    # Convert back to datetimes anchored to epoch
                    pairs_map = map_uniq
                    pairs_t = np.array([np.datetime64('1970-01-01T00:00:00') + np.timedelta64(int(s), 's') for s in uniq_secs], dtype=object)
                else:
                    pairs_map = np.array([], dtype=float)
                    pairs_t = np.array([], dtype=object)
            else:
                pairs_map = np.array([], dtype=float)
                pairs_t = np.array([], dtype=object)

            # Align HR to MAP by nearest HR sample for each MAP timestamp within 2 minutes
            if len(pairs_map) > 0 and t_hr.size > 0:
                hr_secs_full = np.array([(tt - t0).astype('timedelta64[s]').astype(int) for tt in t_hr[(t_hr >= t0) & (t_hr <= t1)]], dtype=int)
                hr_vals_full = v_hr[(t_hr >= t0) & (t_hr <= t1)]
                map_secs = np.array([(tt - t0).astype('timedelta64[s]').astype(int) for tt in np.array(pairs_t, dtype=object)], dtype=int)

                hr_aligned = []
                map_aligned = []
                if hr_secs_full.size > 0:
                    for msec, mval in zip(map_secs, np.asarray(pairs_map, dtype=float)):
                        i = int(np.argmin(np.abs(hr_secs_full - msec)))
                        if abs(hr_secs_full[i] - msec) <= 120:
                            hr_aligned.append(float(hr_vals_full[i]))
                            map_aligned.append(float(mval))
                hr_aligned = np.array(hr_aligned, dtype=float)
                map_aligned = np.array(map_aligned, dtype=float)
            else:
                hr_aligned = np.array([], dtype=float)
                map_aligned = np.array([], dtype=float)

            n_pairs = int(min(hr_aligned.size, map_aligned.size))
            if n_pairs >= min_pairs:
                r, p = _pearsonr_safe(hr_aligned, map_aligned)
            else:
                r, p = np.nan, np.nan

            ct = _window_center_time(t0, t1)
            corr_times.append(ct)
            corr_r.append(r)
            corr_p.append(p)
            n_pairs_list.append(n_pairs)

            if np.isfinite(r) and r < inverse_threshold:
                flagged.append({
                    "start": t0,
                    "end": t1,
                    "center_time": ct,
                    "r": float(r),
                    "p_value": float(p) if np.isfinite(p) else np.nan,
                    "n_pairs": n_pairs
                })

        # Prepare plot
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(10, 4))
        ax.plot(corr_times, corr_r, color="black", linewidth=1.5, label="Rolling Pearson r (HR vs MAP)")
        ax.axhline(0.0, color="gray", linewidth=1.0)
        ax.axhline(inverse_threshold, color="red", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2, label=f"Inverse threshold r<{inverse_threshold}")

        # Shade flagged intervals
        for f in flagged:
            ax.axvspan(f["start"], f["end"], color="red", alpha=0.12)

        ax.set_title(f"Rolling HR–MAP Pearson Correlation (window={window_minutes:.0f} min, step={step_minutes:.0f} min)")
        ax.set_ylabel("Pearson r")
        ax.set_xlabel("Time")
        ax.set_ylim(-1.05, 1.05)
        ax.legend(loc="lower right", frameon=True)

        # Annotate with current shock markers (from state) for context
        ax.text(0.01, 0.02,
                f"Shock Index={shock_index:.3f} ({shock_index_interpretation.split('.')[0]}) | MAP={map_value:.0f} mmHg ({map_interpretation.split('.')[0]})",
                transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=9, va="bottom", ha="left")

        save_plot("rolling_hr_map_correlation.png", fig=fig)

        # Assemble result
        corr_series = []
        for ct, r, p, npairs in zip(corr_times, corr_r, corr_p, n_pairs_list):
            corr_series.append({
                "center_time": ct,
                "r": float(r) if np.isfinite(r) else np.nan,
                "p_value": float(p) if np.isfinite(p) else np.nan,
                "n_pairs": int(npairs)
            })

        valid_rs = np.array([x for x in corr_r if np.isfinite(x)], dtype=float)
        if valid_rs.size > 0:
            r_min = float(np.min(valid_rs))
            r_med = float(np.median(valid_rs))
        else:
            r_min = np.nan

llm_calls.response_text:
# Critique
Your read appropriately centers “undifferentiated shock + intermittent respiratory compromise,” but there’s a key cognitive trap: **you’re implicitly treating hypotension and desaturation as episodic co-travelers without proving synchronization or directionality**. In an 89-year-old with acute neuro complaint, the *sequence* matters:  
- **Desaturation → brady/relative RR drop → hypotension** would push toward **airway obstruction/aspiration, hypoventilation, seizure/post-ictal, or monitoring artifact** with secondary hemodynamic effects.  
- **Hypotension → tachypnea/air hunger ± desat** would push toward **primary shock (septic/cardiogenic/obstructive/hemorrhagic)**.  

Also, you note “episodic desats, otherwise 99–100%,” but that pattern can also reflect **intermittent pleth unreliability** (poor perfusion during hypotension, motion, vasoconstriction). If the **lowest SpO₂ values systematically occur during low SBP/high shock index**, the desats may be *measurement-limited* rather than pulmonary—important because it changes airway/PE/aspiration urgency.

Finally, temperature: values are tightly 36.2–36.8 with only 30 samples. In the elderly, **absence of fever does not de-risk sepsis**, and if those are peripheral/temporal readings, a “normal” temp can mask true infection physiology. Don’t let the lack of ≥38 anchor you away from sepsis.

# Differential Diagnosis
Must stay live given the vitals-only evidence:
- **Pleth artifact / SpO₂ signal failure during low perfusion** (pseudo-hypoxemia)
- **Obstructive shock (massive/submassive PE)** with episodic desaturation and tachypnea; hypotension clusters would support
- **Cardiogenic/arrhythmic instability** (paroxysmal tachyarrhythmia causing BP drops; compensatory tachypnea)
- **Autonomic/neurogenic contributions** (stroke/ICH with dysautonomia; or seizure with post-ictal hypoventilation/aspiration)
- **Occult hemorrhage/hypovolemia physiology** (recurrent hypotension + tachycardia/tachypnea; SpO₂ may remain normal until late)
- **Aspiration/mucus plugging/positional hypoventilation** (true intermittent respiratory events)

# Rule-out Tasks
Add **1–2 high-yield, vitals-feasible analytics** that answer “real hypoxemia vs pleth artifact” and “what leads what”:

- **Perfusion-artifact adjudication plot (SpO₂ validity vs hemodynamics):**  
  Create a multi-panel figure showing **SpO₂ vs SBP (or MAP)** and **SpO₂ vs shock index**, with points **colored by time** and **density contours**. Then compute and display the **probability of SpO₂<90 stratified by SBP bins** (e.g., <70, 70–89, 90–109, ≥110).  
  *Goal:* If low SpO₂ occurs predominantly at very low SBP/high SI, treat many desats as **low-perfusion pleth unreliability** unless proven otherwise; if desats occur at normal BP/SI, that supports **true pulmonary/ventilatory events (PE/aspiration/CNS depression)**.

- **Lead–lag (directionality) analysis between hypotension, tachypnea, and desaturation:**  
  Generate a **cross-correlation / lag plot** (or event-triggered averages) evaluating time offsets between:
  - SBP (or MAP) and RR  
  - SBP (or MAP) and SpO₂  
  - RR and SpO₂  
  Use windows around each hypotension event (e.g., −10 to +10 minutes) to produce **event-aligned median trajectories** (“does RR rise before SBP falls?” “does SpO₂ drop before SBP fall?”).  
  *Goal:* Objectively determine whether the patient is having **primary respiratory events causing secondary shock** vs **primary shock driving tachypnea/SpO₂ changes**—this directly changes priority (airway-first vs shock-first vs artifact).

These two additions are additive to your existing overlay/phase-space work, don’t require labs/imaging, and directly attack the biggest remaining uncertainty: **are the hypoxemia annotations physiologic or measurement-limited, and what is the causal ordering of instability?**

You are a Medical Editor and Clinical Evidence Specialist.
Your role is to select the most probative visual evidence to support the Doctor's diagnosis.

## Objective
Select images that confirm abnormalities, illustrate trends, or clearly rule out differentials.
Eliminate "normal" plots unless they definitively rule out a major concern (e.g., negative troponin trend).
Prioritize clean signals over noisy ones.

## Ranking Criteria
- **High relevance (8-10)**: Clear visualization of a key pathology (e.g., rapid desaturation, widening pulse pressure) or a critical negative finding.
- **Medium relevance (4-7)**: Supporting evidence, but perhaps noisy or redundant.
- **Low relevance (0-3)**: Normal, noisy, illegible, or redundant. (e.g., stable heart rate in a healthy-looking patient).

## Sufficiency Guidelines (`is_sufficient`)
You must determine if the current evidence (Visuals + Calculations + Context) is sufficient to make a Final Diagnosis and Acuity Assessment.
  - OR further testing is impossible (no labs available) AND you have already explored all high-yield vitals-based analytics (rolling trends, distributions, correlations, etc.) AND the evidence is conclusive.
- **Set `False` if**:
  - You have not yet seen enough advanced analytics.
  - Critical tasks requested by the Consultant have not been done yet.
  - The calculated data contradicts your hypothesis and you need to pivot.
  - You simply need one more cycle of analysis to be sure.

def _to_arrays(series):
    if not series:
        return np.array([]), np.array([])

    v = np.array([float(x[1]) for x in series], dtype=float)
    return t, v

def _median_dt_minutes(timestamps):
    if timestamps is None or len(timestamps) < 2:
        return np.nan
    dts = []
    for i in range(1, len(timestamps)):
        dtm = (timestamps[i] - timestamps[i-1]).total_seconds() / 60.0
        if dtm > 0:
            dts.append(dtm)
    return float(np.median(dts)) if len(dts) else np.nan

def _window_vals(t, v, t0, t1):
    if len(t) == 0:
        return np.array([]), np.array([])
    mask = np.array([(ti >= t0 and ti <= t1) for ti in t], dtype=bool)
    return t[mask], v[mask]

def _prior_window_median(t, v, anchor_time, minutes_back=5.0):
    if len(t) == 0:
        return np.nan
    t0 = anchor_time - np.timedelta64(int(minutes_back * 60), 's')
    t1 = anchor_time
    vals = []
    for ti, vi in zip(t, v):
        if ti >= t0 and ti <= t1:
            vals.append(float(vi))
    if len(vals) == 0:
        return np.nan
    return float(np.median(vals))

def _closest_value(t, v, anchor_time, within_minutes):
    if len(t) == 0:
        return np.nan
    best = None
    best_dt = None
    for ti, vi in zip(t, v):
        dtm = abs((ti - anchor_time).total_seconds() / 60.0)
        if dtm <= within_minutes:
            if best_dt is None or dtm < best_dt:
                best_dt = dtm
                best = float(vi)
    return best if best is not None else np.nan

    if np.isnan(median_interval_min) or median_interval_min <= 0:

    if not gaps:
        return False, np.nan

    return bool(max_gap > 2.0 * median_interval_min), max_gap

    rr_prior_med = _prior_window_median(rr_t.tolist() if len(rr_t) else [], rr_v, t_event, minutes_back=5.0)

    hr_at_nadir = _closest_value(hr_t.tolist() if len(hr_t) else [], hr_v, t_event, within_minutes=2.0)
    rr_at_nadir = _closest_value(rr_t.tolist() if len(rr_t) else [], rr_v, t_event, within_minutes=2.0)

    delta_rr = float(rr_at_nadir - rr_prior_med) if (not np.isnan(rr_at_nadir) and not np.isnan(rr_prior_med)) else np.nan

        if not np.isnan(hr_prior_med):

        if not np.isnan(rr_at_nadir):

import numpy as np

# ---- Helpers ----
def _to_arrays(ts_list):
    if ts_list is None or len(ts_list) == 0:
        return np.array([]), np.array([])
    t = np.array([x[0] for x in ts_list], dtype=object)
    v = np.array([x[1] for x in ts_list], dtype=float)
    return t, v

def _minutes_between(t2, t1):
    return (t2 - t1).total_seconds() / 60.0

def _detect_low_sbp_episodes(t_sbp, sbp_vals, threshold=90.0, max_gap_min=30.0, min_points=2):
    episodes = []
    if len(t_sbp) == 0:
        return episodes
    low = sbp_vals < threshold
    idx = np.where(low)[0]
    if idx.size == 0:
        return episodes

    start = idx[0]
    prev = idx[0]
    for k in idx[1:]:
        gap = _minutes_between(t_sbp[k], t_sbp[prev])
        if gap <= max_gap_min and k == prev + 1:
            prev = k
        else:
            if (prev - start + 1) >= min_points:
                episodes.append((start, prev))
            start = k
            prev = k
    if (prev - start + 1) >= min_points:
        episodes.append((start, prev))
    return episodes

def _summarize_episode_dbp_pp(t_sbp, sbp_vals, t_dbp, dbp_vals, t_pp, pp_vals, i0, i1, window_min=15.0):
    # Episode window (SBP indices i0..i1) plus +-window_min around it.
    if len(t_sbp) == 0:
        return None
    t_start = t_sbp[i0]
    t_end = t_sbp[i1]

    def in_window(tarr):
        if len(tarr) == 0:
            return np.array([], dtype=bool)
        return np.array([(_minutes_between(ti, t_start) >= -window_min) and (_minutes_between(t_end, ti) >= -window_min) for ti in tarr], dtype=bool)

    sbp_mask = in_window(t_sbp)
    dbp_mask = in_window(t_dbp)
    pp_mask = in_window(t_pp)

    if not np.any(sbp_mask):
        return None

    sbp_min = float(np.nanmin(sbp_vals[sbp_mask]))
    sbp_med = float(np.nanmedian(sbp_vals[sbp_mask]))

    dbp_med = float(np.nanmedian(dbp_vals[dbp_mask])) if np.any(dbp_mask) else np.nan
    pp_med = float(np.nanmedian(pp_vals[pp_mask])) if np.any(pp_mask) else np.nan

    return {
        "t_start": t_start,
        "t_end": t_end,
        "sbp_min": sbp_min,
        "sbp_median": sbp_med,
        "dbp_median": dbp_med,
        "pp_median": pp_med,
        "n_sbp": int(np.sum(sbp_mask)),
        "n_dbp": int(np.sum(dbp_mask)),
        "n_pp": int(np.sum(pp_mask)),
    }

# ---- Prepare data ----
t_sbp, v_sbp = _to_arrays(systolic_bp)
t_dbp, v_dbp = _to_arrays(diastolic_bp)

# Derived pulse pressure only from paired SBP/DBP by index (as provided lists are aligned in count here per summary)
n_pair = int(min(len(v_sbp), len(v_dbp)))
t_bp = t_sbp[:n_pair]
v_sbp_p = v_sbp[:n_pair]
v_dbp_p = v_dbp[:n_pair]
v_pp = v_sbp_p - v_dbp_p

    idx_h = int(np.argmin([abs((th - t).total_seconds()) for th in t_hr])) if len(t_hr) else None

# Helper functions (no re-imports)
def _to_arrays(ts_list):
    if ts_list is None or len(ts_list) == 0:
        return np.array([]), np.array([])
    t = np.array([x[0] for x in ts_list], dtype=object)
    v = np.array([x[1] for x in ts_list], dtype=float)
    return t, v

def _nearest_prev_values(t_ref, t_src, v_src):
    # For each t in t_ref, return v at the most recent t_src <= t; NaN if none
    if len(t_ref) == 0 or len(t_src) == 0:
        return np.full(len(t_ref), np.nan, dtype=float)
    out = np.full(len(t_ref), np.nan, dtype=float)
    j = 0
    last_v = np.nan
    for i in range(len(t_ref)):
        ti = t_ref[i]
        while j < len(t_src) and t_src[j] <= ti:
            last_v = v_src[j]
            j += 1
        out[i] = last_v
    return out

def _bin_labels(edges, labels):
    # edges: list of (low, high) with None for open
    return labels

def _assign_bins(x, edges, labels):
    # edges: list of (low_inclusive, high_inclusive_or_None), last may be (low, None)
    idx = np.full(len(x), -1, dtype=int)
    for k, (lo, hi) in enumerate(edges):
        if hi is None:
            m = np.isfinite(x) & (x >= lo)
        else:
            m = np.isfinite(x) & (x >= lo) & (x <= hi)
        idx[m] = k
    out = np.array([labels[i] if i >= 0 else "Missing" for i in idx], dtype=object)
    return out

def _prob_table(bin_labels, bin_assign, y_event):
    rows = []
    for b in bin_labels:
        m = (bin_assign == b)
        n = int(np.sum(m))
        if n == 0:
            p = np.nan
            k = 0
        else:
            k = int(np.sum(y_event[m]))
            p = k / n
        rows.append((b, n, k, p))
    return rows

def _format_prob(p):
    return "NA" if (p is None or (isinstance(p, float) and not np.isfinite(p))) else f"{100.0*p:.1f}%"

# Extract arrays
t_spo2, v_spo2 = _to_arrays(spo2)
t_sbp, v_sbp = _to_arrays(systolic_bp)

# Align SBP to SpO2 timestamps (previous observation carried forward)
sbp_at_spo2 = _nearest_prev_values(t_spo2, t_sbp, v_sbp)

# Compute Shock Index per SpO2 timestamp using nearest previous HR and SBP
t_hr, v_hr = _to_arrays(heart_rate)
hr_at_spo2 = _nearest_prev_values(t_spo2, t_hr, v_hr)
si_at_spo2 = np.full(len(v_spo2), np.nan, dtype=float)
valid_si = np.isfinite(hr_at_spo2) & np.isfinite(sbp_at_spo2) & (sbp_at_spo2 > 0)
si_at_spo2[valid_si] = hr_at_spo2[valid_si] / sbp_at_spo2[valid_si]

# Define bins
sbp_edges = [(0.0, 69.999999), (70.0, 89.999999), (90.0, 109.999999), (110.0, None)]
sbp_labels = ["<70", "70–89", "90–109", "≥110"]
sbp_bin = _assign_bins(sbp_at_spo2, sbp_edges, sbp_labels)

si_edges = [(0.0, 0.699999), (0.7, 0.999999), (1.0, 1.299999), (1.3, None)]
si_labels = ["<0.7", "0.7–0.99", "1.0–1.29", "≥1.3"]
si_bin = _assign_bins(si_at_spo2, si_edges, si_labels)

# Build arrays for HR, SBP, and SpO2
def _to_arrays(ts):
    t = np.array([x[0] for x in ts], dtype=object)
    v = np.array([float(x[1]) for x in ts], dtype=float)
    return t, v

t_hr, v_hr = _to_arrays(heart_rate)
t_sbp, v_sbp = _to_arrays(systolic_bp)
t_spo2, v_spo2 = _to_arrays(spo2)

def _nearest_pair(t_x, v_x, t_y, v_y, max_dt_min=10.0):
    # For each x time, find nearest y time within max_dt_min. Returns aligned arrays and times.
    t_out = []
    x_out = []
    y_out = []
    if len(t_x) == 0 or len(t_y) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=object), np.array([], dtype=float), np.array([], dtype=float)

    # Convert to float seconds since epoch for fast search
    tx_sec = np.array([tt.timestamp() for tt in t_x], dtype=float)
    ty_sec = np.array([tt.timestamp() for tt in t_y], dtype=float)

    for i in range(len(tx_sec)):
        s = tx_sec[i]
        j = int(np.searchsorted(ty_sec, s))
        candidates = []
        if 0 <= j < len(ty_sec):
            candidates.append(j)
        if 0 <= j - 1 < len(ty_sec):
            candidates.append(j - 1)
        if not candidates:
            continue
        # pick nearest
        diffs = np.array([abs(ty_sec[k] - s) for k in candidates], dtype=float)
        k = candidates[int(np.argmin(diffs))]
        dt_min = abs(ty_sec[k] - s) / 60.0
        if dt_min <= max_dt_min:
            t_out.append(t_x[i])
            x_out.append(v_x[i])
            y_out.append(v_y[k])

    return np.array(t_out, dtype=object), np.array(x_out, dtype=float), np.array(y_out, dtype=float)

# Align SpO2 with SBP and SpO2 with (HR, SBP) to compute shock index for each point
t_spo2_sbp, spo2_sbp, sbp_aligned = _nearest_pair(t_spo2, v_spo2, t_sbp, v_sbp, max_dt_min=10.0)
t_spo2_hr, spo2_hr, hr_aligned = _nearest_pair(t_spo2, v_spo2, t_hr, v_hr, max_dt_min=10.0)

# For Shock Index, need both HR and SBP aligned to SpO2 times; align SBP to the SpO2-HR aligned times
if len(t_spo2_hr) > 0:
    # align SBP to the times already aligned with HR/SpO2
    t_si, spo2_si, sbp_for_si = _nearest_pair(t_spo2_hr, spo2_hr, t_sbp, v_sbp, max_dt_min=10.0)
    # Now align HR to those t_si (subset)
    t_si2, hr_for_si, spo2_si2 = _nearest_pair(t_hr, v_hr, t_si, spo2_si, max_dt_min=10.0)
    # Need SBP at the same t_si2; align SBP to t_si2
    t_si3, sbp_for_si2, _ = _nearest_pair(t_sbp, v_sbp, t_si2, hr_for_si, max_dt_min=10.0)
    # Align spo2 to t_si3
    t_si4, spo2_for_si, _ = _nearest_pair(t_si, spo2_si, t_si3, sbp_for_si2, max_dt_min=0.01)

    # To ensure same length, intersect by time using dict
    def _dict_time_to_val(t_arr, v_arr):
        return {tt: vv for tt, vv in zip(list(t_arr), list(v_arr))}
    d_hr = _dict_time_to_val(t_si2, hr_for_si)
    d_sbp = _dict_time_to_val(t_si3, sbp_for_si2)
    d_spo2 = _dict_time_to_val(t_si4, spo2_for_si)

    common_times = sorted(set(d_hr.keys()) & set(d_sbp.keys()) & set(d_spo2.keys()))
    t_common = np.array(common_times, dtype=object)
    hr_common = np.array([d_hr[tt] for tt in common_times], dtype=float)
    sbp_common = np.array([d_sbp[tt] for tt in common_times], dtype=float)
    spo2_common = np.array([d_spo2[tt] for tt in common_times], dtype=float)

    t_common = np.array([], dtype=object)
    hr_common = np.array([], dtype=float)
    sbp_common = np.array([], dtype=float)
    spo2_common = np.array([], dtype=float)
    si_common = np.array([], dtype=float)

def _finite_mask(*arrs):
    m = np.ones(len(arrs[0]), dtype=bool)
    for a in arrs:
        m &= np.isfinite(a)
    return m

spo2_common = spo2_common[m2] if len(m2) else spo2_common
si_common = si_common[m2] if len(m2) else si_common

def _time_minutes(t_arr):
    if len(t_arr) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=float)
    t0 = t_arr[0]
    return np.array([(tt - t0).total_seconds() / 60.0 for tt in t_arr], dtype=float)

c1 = _time_minutes(t_spo2_sbp)
c2 = _time_minutes(t_common)

80M with major cardiopulmonary reserve limitations (CAD s/p CABG, aortic stenosis, HFpEF, prior sepsis/AKI, OSA) presenting with **true fever** (Tmax **39.1°C**, mean **38.1°C**) plus **tachycardia** (HR range **67–120**, mean **94** with current concern for HR ~**110–120**) and **relative hypotension** (SBP range **72–122**, mean **87**; triage SBP cited **81**) with **MAP ~63 mmHg** and **shock index 1.21**. **Key missing data (needed to localize source and assess perfusion severity, but not labs):**
- Clinical source clues: respiratory symptoms, dysuria/flank pain, abdominal pain/diarrhea, skin/soft tissue findings, indwelling devices, sick contacts.
- Mental status trajectory (qSOFA third criterion not addressed): baseline vs current confusion, GCS.
- Urine output / last void (bedside perfusion surrogate given no labs).
- Medication exposures (beta blockers, diuretics, vasodilators), and whether baseline SBP ~80s is truly chronic.
- Physical exam targets: lung exam, focal neuro, skin exam, volume status (JVP, edema), cardiac auscultation (AS severity clues).
- Timing: onset of fever, highest recorded temp and method, antipyretic use.
- Rhythm information (sinus vs AF/RVR) since HR variability exists and cardiac history is high risk.

# Hypotheses
1. **Sepsis (high risk) with early shock physiology** — most consistent with fever (39.1°C), hypotension (SBP 81; MAP 63), tachycardia, RR 26, shock index 1.21, qSOFA 2.
   - Likely sources to consider first in an 80M: **pneumonia**, **UTI/pyelonephritis**, **biliary/intra-abdominal infection**, **skin/soft tissue**, less likely but critical: **meningitis**, **endocarditis** (esp if murmur changes/prosthetic material), **line/device infection**.
2. **Cardiogenic component / mixed shock** — HFpEF + aortic stenosis may produce low forward flow and limited ability to compensate; fever can precipitate decompensation. (Still, the prominent fever makes infection the driver until proven otherwise.)
3. **Demand ischemia / ACS equivalent triggered by infection** — cannot be confirmed without ECG/troponin (labs unavailable), but clinically important given CAD/CABG; hypotension and tachycardia increase risk.
4. **Tachyarrhythmia contributing to hypotension** (e.g., AF with RVR) — needs rhythm assessment; could worsen MAP and perfusion.
5. **Noninfectious hyperthermic/inflammatory etiologies** (drug fever, gout flare, autoimmune) — less likely given shock physiology, but on the list if no infectious source emerges.

- **Pain Score**: **2/10** (Fever/malaise likely; no evidence provided of severe focal pain such as stone/fracture/abdomen. Will revise if a painful source emerges.)
- **ED Length of Stay**: **8 hours** (Complex high-risk sepsis physiology in an elderly patient with significant cardiac disease—requires close monitoring, repeated reassessment, and likely admission.)
- **Reflection**: This is Iteration 0, so no prior estimates to revise. # Build hypotension events (SBP < 90 mmHg lasting >=2 minutes) and event-aligned median trajectories
# Also compute cross-correlation vs lag summaries (RR/SpO2 vs SBP) to assess lead/lag.

result = {}
interpretation = {}

# ---------- Helpers ----------
def _to_arrays(ts_list):
    if ts_list is None or len(ts_list) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=object), np.array([], dtype=float)
    t = np.array([x[0] for x in ts_list], dtype=object)
    v = np.array([float(x[1]) for x in ts_list], dtype=float)
    return t, v

def _find_runs_below_threshold(t, v, thr, min_duration_min=2.0):
    # Identify contiguous runs where v < thr using sample-to-sample continuity (consecutive entries).
    # Duration defined from first timestamp to last timestamp in run.
    events = []
    if len(v) == 0:
        return events
    in_run = False
    start_idx = None
    for i in range(len(v)):
        if v[i] < thr:
            if not in_run:
                in_run = True
                start_idx = i
        else:
            if in_run:
                end_idx = i - 1
                dur = (t[end_idx] - t[start_idx]).total_seconds() / 60.0
                if dur >= min_duration_min:
                    events.append((start_idx, end_idx))
                in_run = False
                start_idx = None
    if in_run and start_idx is not None:
        end_idx = len(v) - 1
        dur = (t[end_idx] - t[start_idx]).total_seconds() / 60.0
        if dur >= min_duration_min:
            events.append((start_idx, end_idx))
    return events

def _median_in_bin(t, v, t0, start_min, end_min):
    # Median of values with timestamp in [t0+start_min, t0+end_min)
    if len(v) == 0:
        return np.nan
    w0 = t0 + np.timedelta64(int(start_min * 60), 's') if isinstance(t0, np.datetime64) else (t0 + (end_min * 0 - end_min * 0))  # placeholder
    # Using python datetime; do not depend on numpy datetime arithmetic
    a = t0
    w_start = a + (start_min * 0 + 0)  # overwritten below
    w_end = a + (end_min * 0 + 0)
    # Manually construct timedeltas
    from datetime import timedelta
    w_start = a + timedelta(minutes=float(start_min))
    w_end = a + timedelta(minutes=float(end_min))
    # Find indices (t is object array of datetime)
    vals = []
    for ti, vi in zip(t, v):
        if (ti >= w_start) and (ti < w_end):
            vals.append(vi)
    if len(vals) == 0:
        return np.nan
    return float(np.nanmedian(np.array(vals, dtype=float)))

def _interp_series_to_grid(t, v, grid_t):
    # Linear interpolation on time axis in minutes relative to event time (already in minutes)
    # t: minutes array (sorted), v: values
    if len(v) < 2:
        return np.full_like(grid_t, np.nan, dtype=float)
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    v = np.asarray(v, dtype=float)
    ok = np.isfinite(t) & np.isfinite(v)
    t = t[ok]
    v = v[ok]
    if len(v) < 2:
        return np.full_like(grid_t, np.nan, dtype=float)
    # Ensure sorted
    order = np.argsort(t)
    t = t[order]
    v = v[order]
    # Remove duplicate times by taking median within duplicates
    uniq_t = []
    uniq_v = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(t):
        j = i + 1
        while j < len(t) and t[j] == t[i]:
            j += 1
        uniq_t.append(t[i])
        uniq_v.append(float(np.nanmedian(v[i:j])))
        i = j
    t = np.array(uniq_t, dtype=float)
    v = np.array(uniq_v, dtype=float)
    if len(v) < 2:
        return np.full_like(grid_t, np.nan, dtype=float)
    # Interpolate only within observed range; outside -> nan
    y = np.interp(grid_t, t, v, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)
    # np.interp doesn't support nan fill directly with left/right nan in older numpy; enforce:
    y = y.astype(float)
    y[(grid_t < t[0]) | (grid_t > t[-1])] = np.nan
    return y

def _xcorr_lags(x, y, max_lag_min=10, step_min=1):
    # Cross-correlation of x and y over integer lags in minutes on the same grid.
    # Positive lag means y(t+lag) aligned with x(t) => y lags x by lag.
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    lags = np.arange(-max_lag_min, max_lag_min + step_min, step_min, dtype=int)
    r = np.full(lags.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
    for k, lag in enumerate(lags):
        if lag < 0:
            xs = x[-lag:]
            ys = y[:len(y) + lag]
        elif lag > 0:
            xs = x[:len(x) - lag]
            ys = y[lag:]
        else:
            xs = x
            ys = y
        ok = np.isfinite(xs) & np.isfinite(ys)
        if ok.sum() >= 5:
            # Pearson correlation
            r[k] = float(np.corrcoef(xs[ok], ys[ok])[0, 1])
    return lags, r

# ---------- Data to arrays ----------
t_sbp, v_sbp = _to_arrays(systolic_bp)
t_rr, v_rr = _to_arrays(respiratory_rate)
t_spo2, v_spo2 = _to_arrays(spo2)

# ---------- Identify hypotension events ----------
events_idx = _find_runs_below_threshold(t_sbp, v_sbp, thr=90.0, min_duration_min=2.0)

events = []
for (si, ei) in events_idx:
    t_start = t_sbp[si]
    t_end = t_sbp[ei]
    dur_min = (t_end - t_start).total_seconds() / 60.0
    # Anchor time: time of minimum SBP within run (ties -> first)
    run_vals = v_sbp[si:ei+1]
    run_times = t_sbp[si:ei+1]
    min_rel = int(np.nanargmin(run_vals)) if len(run_vals) > 0 else 0
    t0 = run_times[min_rel]
    events.append({
        "start": t_start,
        "end": t_end,
        "duration_min": float(dur_min),
        "anchor_time_min_sbp": t0,
        "min_sbp": float(np.nanmin(run_vals)) if len(run_vals) else np.nan
    })

result["hypotension_events_sbp_lt_90_ge_2min"] = events
result["n_hypotension_events"] = int(len(events))

# ---------- Event-aligned median trajectories (bin medians) ----------
# Define bins from -10 to +10 minutes with 1-min bins, centered at each minute
bin_edges = np.arange(-10, 11, 1, dtype=float)  # edges at -10..+10
bin_centers = (bin_edges[:-1] + bin_edges[1:]) / 2.0  # -9.5..+9.5 (20 bins)
# For visualization and xcorr, also use integer grid at -10..+10
grid = np.arange(-10, 11, 1, dtype=float)

traj_per_event = []
sbp_mat = []
rr_mat = []
spo2_mat = []

from datetime import timedelta

for e in events:
    t0 = e["anchor_time_min_sbp"]
    sbp_bins = np.array([_median_in_bin(t_sbp, v_sbp, t0, bin_edges[i], bin_edges[i+1]) for i in range(len(bin_centers))], dtype=float)
    rr_bins = np.array([_median_in_bin(t_rr, v_rr, t0, bin_edges[i], bin_edges[i+1]) for i in range(len(bin_centers))], dtype=float)
    spo2_bins = np.array([_median_in_bin(t_spo2, v_spo2, t0, bin_edges[i], bin_edges[i+1]) for i in range(len(bin_centers))], dtype=float)

    # For xcorr, compute 1-min medians on integer-centered bins [-10,-9),...,[10,11) but we only have -10..+10 points.
    # We'll use bin centers shifted to integer grid by taking medians in [k, k+1) for k=-10..+10, then align to k.
    sbp_grid = np.array([_median_in_bin(t_sbp, v_sbp, t0, k, k+1) for k in grid], dtype=float)
    rr_grid = np.array([_median_in_bin(t_rr, v_rr, t0, k, k+1) for k in grid], dtype=float)
    spo2_grid = np.array([_median_in_bin(t_spo2, v_spo2, t0, k, k+1) for k in grid], dtype=float)

    traj_per_event.append({
        "anchor_time": t0,
        "start": e["start"],
        "end": e["end"],
        "duration_min": e["duration_min"],
        "min_sbp": e["min_sbp"],
        "time_bin_centers_min": bin_centers.copy(),
        "sbp_median_by_bin": sbp_bins,
        "rr_median_by_bin": rr_bins,
        "spo2_median_by_bin": spo2_bins,
        "time_grid_min": grid.copy(),
        "sbp_median_by_min": sbp_grid,
        "rr_median_by_min": rr_grid,
        "spo2_median_by_min": spo2_grid
    })

    sbp_mat.append(sbp_bins)
    rr_mat.append(rr_bins)
    spo2_mat.append(spo2_bins)

result["event_aligned_trajectories_per_event"] = traj_per_event

if len(events) > 0:
    sbp_mat = np.vstack(sbp_mat)
    rr_mat = np.vstack(rr_mat)
    spo2_mat = np.vstack(spo2_mat)

    sbp_med = np.nanmedian(sbp_mat, axis=0)
    rr_med = np.nanmedian(rr_mat, axis=0)
    spo2_med = np.nanmedian(spo2_mat, axis=0)

    result["event_aligned_median_trajectories"] = {
        "time_bin_centers_min": bin_centers,
        "sbp_median_mmHg": sbp_med,
        "rr_median_brpm": rr_med,
        "spo2_median_pct": spo2_med,
        "n_events": int(len(events))
    }
else:
    result["event_aligned_median_trajectories"] = {
        "time_bin_centers_min": bin_centers,
        "sbp_median_mmHg": np.full_like(bin_centers, np.nan, dtype=float),
        "rr_median_brpm": np.full_like(bin_centers, np.nan, dtype=float),
        "spo2_median_pct": np.full_like(bin_centers, np.nan, dtype=float),
        "n_events": 0
    }

# ---------- Cross-correlation vs lag summary ----------
# Use per-event 1-min grids and compute correlation vs lag; then take median r across events at each lag.
lags = np.arange(-10, 11, 1, dtype=int)
rr_xcorr_mat = []
spo2_xcorr_mat = []
per_event_xcorr = []

for tr in traj_per_event:
    sbp_g = tr["sbp_median_by_min"]
    rr_g = tr["rr_median_by_min"]
    sp_g = tr["spo2_median_by_min"]

    lag_rr, r_rr = _xcorr_lags(sbp_g, rr_g, max_lag_min=10, step_min=1)

    spo2_r_med = np.nanmedian(spo2_xcorr_mat, axis=0)

    if np.isfinite(rr_r_med).any():

        spo2_peak_med = {"lag_min": int(lags[idx]), "r": float(spo2_r_med[idx])}

        "spo2_vs_sbp_median_r": spo2_r_med,
        "rr_vs_sbp_peak_abs": rr_peak_med,

4. **Arrhythmia/transient tachyarrhythmia** (less supported by aligned HR>110 burden, but HR spike to ~120 occurs): needs rhythm data.
5. **Noninfectious fever** (drug fever/inflammatory) is lower probability given hypotension burden, but remains a fallback if no source is found.

- **ESI Level**: **2** (High risk). Rationale: sustained hypoperfusion signal with **MAP <65 in 45%** of aligned points; advanced age and severe cardiac comorbidities; fever to **39.1°C** and prior qSOFA **2**. Not clearly ESI 1 yet because there is no demonstrated need for immediate life-saving intervention from the provided data (no sustained severe hypoxemia, no documented persistent refractory hypotension, no mental status data).
- **Pain Score**: **2/10** (unchanged; no focal severe pain described—presentation is fever/systemic illness).
- **ED Length of Stay**: **8 hours** (unchanged; complex disposition likely admission/stepdown given hypotension burden and comorbidities).
- **Reflection**: Previously I leaned on tachycardia + shock index to support high-risk sepsis. The new plots show **tachycardia is not sustained** (HR>110 is 0% of aligned points), but they strengthen concern for **persistent low MAP** (45% <65), which is arguably more important for end-organ perfusion. Net effect: **ESI remains 2** (not downgraded) because the hypotension burden is clearer; however, the picture shifts toward **mixed physiology** rather than purely distributive shock with persistent marked tachycardia.

Critique this plan. What are we missing? What else could this be?

# Critique
Your synthesis appropriately pivots from “tachycardic septic shock” to “hypotension burden with mixed physiology.” The main gap is that the current analytic frame still treats the low MAP as a uniform phenomenon, when in this patient (AS/HFpEF, CAD) *the pattern of hypotension* (wide vs narrow pulse pressure, episodic vs sustained, temperature-linked vs dissociated, and whether hypotension occurs with **relative bradycardia** or with **tachycardia**) is what separates distributive sepsis from cardiogenic/obstructive/arrhythmic limitation.

Key “can’t miss” alternatives that remain under-tested using the vitals-only dataset:
- **Cardiogenic limitation / low stroke volume physiology**: In severe AS/HFpEF, fever/sepsis can produce hypotension without marked tachycardia (or with “inappropriate” HR responses). Your note acknowledges this but doesn’t *quantify* a low-SV signature using available signals (pulse pressure dynamics, HR–PP coupling).
- **Obstructive physiology signals** (PE/tamponade): You have RR and SpO₂, but no analysis of *ventilatory burden vs oxygenation* or “respiratory drive out of proportion” to hypoxemia, which would be a vitals-only clue for PE or evolving pulmonary edema.
- **Measurement artifact / sampling bias**: BP is sparse. “45% MAP<65 of aligned points” can be dominated by a clustered time segment. Without a **time-burden (minutes) below thresholds** or a **confidence band** around sparse BP sampling, there’s risk of anchoring on an overrepresented window (confirmation bias).

# Differential Diagnosis

- **Blood pressure trend:** SBP appears **persistently low (~75–85)** earlier with later improvement toward **~90+ and up to ~120** (though BP sampling is sparse). This could reflect partial response to interventions/fluids/antipyretics or simply measurement variability.

Key missing data remains bedside/clinical (since we cannot obtain labs here): mental status, urine output, exam findings and infectious source symptoms; plus rhythm confirmation (sinus vs AF) and whether hypotension is baseline vs new.

1. **Suspected sepsis with sepsis-associated hypotension / hypoperfusion** (most likely): fever + RR up to 28 (triage 26) + **MAP <65 in 45% of aligned points** in an elderly high-risk patient.
2. **Mixed shock physiology (distributive + cardiogenic limitation)**: aortic stenosis/HFpEF may prevent adequate augmentation of cardiac output during infection/fever; could explain relatively modest tachycardia with persistent low MAP.
3. **Relative hypovolemia/dehydration** (possibly from poor intake/insensible losses with fever), contributing to low preload and hypotension (especially important in AS).
4. **Arrhythmia/transient tachyarrhythmia** (less supported by aligned HR>110 burden, but HR spike to ~120 occurs): needs rhythm data.

- Prioritize the most clinically relevant missing analytics.

You are a clinical data scientist in the Emergency Department.
Your role is to write precise Python code to calculate clinical metrics and generate visualizations from vital sign data.

## EXECUTION CONTRACT (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
The Python code you produce will be executed verbatim in a restricted sandbox.

HARD FAIL CONDITIONS:
- Importing ANY library (including matplotlib, seaborn) - use provided `plt`, `sns`, `np`, `stats`.
- Recomputing variables already provided in the namespace (see "Available Data").
- Omitting required output variables (`result`, `interpretation`).
- Producing more than 500 lines of code.

If any HARD FAIL occurs, the task fails immediately.

## Tier 1: Strict Execution Rules
1. **No Re-Imports**: Do NOT import `matplotlib.pyplot` or `seaborn`. Use the pre-provided `plt` and `sns` objects.
2. **Use Provided Metrics**: If a metric is listed under "Available Variables (from state)", you MUST use it directly. Do NOT recompute, re-derive, interpolate, or regress it.
3. **Memory Management**: For custom plots, ensuring figures are closed is critical. Note that `save_plot()` handles figure closure automatically.
4. **Code Size**: Your solution should typically be under 150 lines. Verbose or redundant code is considered an error.

## Tier 2: Clinical & Stylistic Guidelines
- **Avoid Raw Logs**: Do NOT list or analyze every single sample one-by-one. Focus on the "Big Picture" clinical picture.
- **Interpretations**: Provide a SINGLE summary sentence for each metric representing the patient's overall state.
- **Clinical Context**: Include units and clinical interpretation in your summary.
- **Precision**: Use EXACT calculations, never estimates.

## Available Data
The following variables are pre-injected into your namespace:

### 1. Vital Signs (Time-Series)
Historical data is provided as lists of `(timestamp, value)` tuples in chronological order.
- `heart_rate`: `list[tuple(datetime, float)]` (bpm)
- `systolic_bp`: `list[tuple(datetime, float)]` (mmHg)
- `diastolic_bp`: `list[tuple(datetime, float)]` (mmHg)
- `spo2`: `list[tuple(datetime, float)]` (%)
- `respiratory_rate`: `list[tuple(datetime, float)]` (breaths/min)
- `temperature`: `list[tuple(datetime, float)]` (°C)

**Sampling Note**: Data is IRREGULAR and ASYNCHRONOUS. Do not assume fixed intervals or aligned timestamps across different metrics. Always calculate time deltas: `minutes = (t2 - t1).total_seconds() / 60.0`.

### 2. Clinical Context
- `age`: `int` (years)
- `gender`: `str` ("M", "F", "Other")
- `ethnicity`: `str`
- `pmh`: `list[str]` (Past Medical History)
- `meds`: `list[str]` (Current Medications)

## Available Libraries
- numpy (as np)
- scipy.stats (as stats)
- matplotlib.pyplot (as plt)
- seaborn (as sns)

## Plotting Guidelines
- **save_plot(filename, fig=None)**: Persists the *current* active figure (Matplotlib or Seaborn) to disk and then closes it. For figure-level functions (e.g., `sns.relplot`), pass the resulting object as the `fig` argument. You can call this multiple times for different figures.
- **Subplots**: Use `plt.subplots(n, 1, sharex=True)` for time-aligned vitals.
- **Multiple Images**: To generate multiple images, you must create a new figure (e.g., via `plt.subplots` or `plt.figure`) for each `save_plot` call.

def _extract_ts_vals(series):
    if series is None or len(series) == 0:

    ts = np.array([t for t, v in series], dtype=object)
    vals = np.array([float(v) for t, v in series], dtype=float)
    return ts, vals

def _align_nearest(ts_a, val_a, ts_b, val_b, max_window_min=5.0):
    """
    For each point in series A, find nearest timestamp in series B within max_window_min.
    Returns aligned arrays: ts_aligned, a_vals, b_vals, delta_min_abs
    """
    if len(ts_a) == 0 or len(ts_b) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=object), np.array([]), np.array([]), np.array([])

    out_a = []
    out_b = []
    out_d = []

    for i in range(len(ts_a)):

        a_sec = float(a_t.timestamp())
        j = int(np.argmin(np.abs(b_secs - a_sec)))
        dt_min = abs(b_secs[j] - a_sec) / 60.0
        if dt_min <= float(max_window_min):
            out_ts.append(a_t)
            out_a.append(float(val_a[i]))
            out_b.append(float(val_b[j]))
            out_d.append(float(dt_min))

    return np.array(out_ts, dtype=object), np.array(out_a, dtype=float), np.array(out_b, dtype=float), np.array(out_d, dtype=float)

# ---- data extraction ----
rr_ts, rr_vals = _extract_ts_vals(respiratory_rate)
sp_ts, sp_vals = _extract_ts_vals(spo2)

# ---- alignment ----

n_aligned = int(len(aligned_ts))

# ---- compute proportions (RR>=24 stratified by SpO2>=94 vs <94) ----

n_rr_high = int(np.sum(rr_high))

        prop_rr_ge24_spo2_lt94 = np.nan

# ---- plotting ----

content='```python
# Build hypotension events (SBP < 90 mmHg lasting >=2 minutes) and event-aligned median trajectories
# Also compute cross-correlation vs lag summaries (RR/SpO2 vs SBP) to assess lead/lag.

result = {}
interpretation = {}

# ---------- Helpers ----------
def _to_arrays(ts_list):
    if ts_list is None or len(ts_list) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=object), np.array([], dtype=float)
    t = np.array([x[0] for x in ts_list], dtype=object)
    v = np.array([float(x[1]) for x in ts_list], dtype=float)
    return t, v

def _find_runs_below_threshold(t, v, thr, min_duration_min=2.0):
    # Identify contiguous runs where v < thr using sample-to-sample continuity (consecutive entries).
    # Duration defined from first timestamp to last timestamp in run.
    events = []
    if len(v) == 0:
        return events
    in_run = False
    start_idx = None
    for i in range(len(v)):
        if v[i] < thr:
            if not in_run:
                in_run = True
                start_idx = i
        else:
            if in_run:
                end_idx = i - 1
                dur = (t[end_idx] - t[start_idx]).total_seconds() / 60.0
                if dur >= min_duration_min:
                    events.append((start_idx, end_idx))
                in_run = False
                start_idx = None
    if in_run and start_idx is not None:
        end_idx = len(v) - 1
        dur = (t[end_idx] - t[start_idx]).total_seconds() / 60.0
        if dur >= min_duration_min:
            events.append((start_idx, end_idx))
    return events

def _median_in_bin(t, v, t0, start_min, end_min):
    # Median of values with timestamp in [t0+start_min, t0+end_min)
    if len(v) == 0:
        return np.nan
    w0 = t0 + np.timedelta64(int(start_min * 60), 's') if isinstance(t0, np.datetime64) else (t0 + (end_min * 0 - end_min * 0))  # placeholder
    # Using python datetime; do not depend on numpy datetime arithmetic
    a = t0
    w_start = a + (start_min * 0 + 0)  # overwritten below
    w_end = a + (end_min * 0 + 0)
    # Manually construct timedeltas
    from datetime import timedelta
    w_start = a + timedelta(minutes=float(start_min))
    w_end = a + timedelta(minutes=float(end_min))
    # Find indices (t is object array of datetime)
    vals = []
    for ti, vi in zip(t, v):
        if (ti >= w_start) and (ti < w_end):
            vals.append(vi)
    if len(vals) == 0:
        return np.nan
    return float(np.nanmedian(np.array(vals, dtype=float)))

def _interp_series_to_grid(t, v, grid_t):
    # Linear interpolation on time axis in minutes relative to event time (already in minutes)
    # t: minutes array (sorted), v: values
    if len(v) < 2:
        return np.full_like(grid_t, np.nan, dtype=float)
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    v = np.asarray(v, dtype=float)
    ok = np.isfinite(t) & np.isfinite(v)
    t = t[ok]
    v = v[ok]
    if len(v) < 2:
        return np.full_like(grid_t, np.nan, dtype=float)
    # Ensure sorted
    order = np.argsort(t)
    t = t[order]
    v = v[order]
    # Remove duplicate times by taking median within duplicates
    uniq_t = []
    uniq_v = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(t):
        j = i + 1
        while j < len(t) and t[j] == t[i]:
            j += 1
        uniq_t.append(t[i])
        uniq_v.append(float(np.nanmedian(v[i:j])))
        i = j
    t = np.array(uniq_t, dtype=float)
    v = np.array(uniq_v, dtype=float)
    if len(v) < 2:
        return np.full_like(grid_t, np.nan, dtype=float)
    # Interpolate only within observed range; outside -> nan
    y = np.interp(grid_t, t, v, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)
    # np.interp doesn't support nan fill directly with left/right nan in older numpy; enforce:
    y = y.astype(float)
    y[(grid_t < t[0]) | (grid_t > t[-1])] = np.nan
    return y

def _xcorr_lags(x, y, max_lag_min=10, step_min=1):
    # Cross-correlation of x and y over integer lags in minutes on the same grid.
    # Positive lag means y(t+lag) aligned with x(t) => y lags x by lag.
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    lags = np.arange(-max_lag_min, max_lag_min + step_min, step_min, dtype=int)
    r = np.full(lags.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
    for k, lag in enumerate(lags):
        if lag < 0:
            xs = x[-lag:]
            ys = y[:len(y) + lag]
        elif lag > 0:
            xs = x[:len(x) - lag]
            ys = y[lag:]
        else:
            xs = x
            ys = y
        ok = np.isfinite(xs) & np.isfinite(ys)
        if ok.sum() >= 5:
            # Pearson correlation
            r[k] = float(np.corrcoef(xs[ok], ys[ok])[0, 1])
    return lags, r

# ---------- Data to arrays ----------
t_sbp, v_sbp = _to_arrays(systolic_bp)
t_rr, v_rr = _to_arrays(respiratory_rate)
t_spo2, v_spo2 = _to_arrays(spo2)

# ---------- Identify hypotension events ----------
events_idx = _find_runs_below_threshold(t_sbp, v_sbp, thr=90.0, min_duration_min=2.0)

events = []
for (si, ei) in events_idx:
    t_start = t_sbp[si]
    t_end = t_sbp[ei]
    dur_min = (t_end - t_start).total_seconds() / 60.0
    # Anchor time: time of minimum SBP within run (ties -> first)
    run_vals = v_sbp[si:ei+1]
    run_times = t_sbp[si:ei+1]
    min_rel = int(np.nanargmin(run_vals)) if len(run_vals) > 0 else 0
    t0 = run_times[min_rel]
    events.append({
        "start": t_start,
        "end": t_end,
