# Phase-space plot: Pulse Pressure vs MAP colored by Temperature, time-aligned to BP samples
# Also report clustering of low MAP with narrow pulse pressure.

# --- helpers (no re-imports) ---
def _extract_ts_vals(ts_list):
    if ts_list is None:
        return [], []
    t = [x[0] for x in ts_list]
    v = [float(x[1]) for x in ts_list]
    return t, v

def _nearest_value(t_query, t_list, v_list):
    # returns (value, abs_minutes) for nearest timestamp in t_list; None if no data
    if not t_list:
        return None, None
    # linear scan (lists are modest size); avoids extra dependencies
    best_i = 0
    best_dt = abs((t_list[0] - t_query).total_seconds())
    for i in range(1, len(t_list)):
        dt = abs((t_list[i] - t_query).total_seconds())
        if dt < best_dt:
            best_dt = dt
            best_i = i
    return v_list[best_i], best_dt / 60.0

# --- prepare BP-aligned dataset ---
t_sbp, v_sbp = _extract_ts_vals(systolic_bp)
t_dbp, v_dbp = _extract_ts_vals(diastolic_bp)
t_temp, v_temp = _extract_ts_vals(temperature)

bp_times = []
sbp_aligned = []
dbp_aligned = []
temp_aligned = []
temp_dt_min = []

# align by SBP timestamps; require a DBP within a reasonable window to compute PP & MAP
# (asynchronous sampling: use nearest DBP; keep if within 10 minutes)
MAX_ALIGN_MIN = 10.0

for i, t in enumerate(t_sbp):
    dbp_val, dbp_dt = _nearest_value(t, t_dbp, v_dbp)
    if dbp_val is None or dbp_dt is None or dbp_dt > MAX_ALIGN_MIN:
        continue
    sbp_val = v_sbp[i]
    pp_val = sbp_val - dbp_val
    map_val = (sbp_val + 2.0 * dbp_val) / 3.0

    tmp_val, tmp_dt = _nearest_value(t, t_temp, v_temp)
    # temperature may be sparse; allow up to 60 minutes alignment; otherwise set NaN
    if tmp_val is None or tmp_dt is None or tmp_dt > 60.0:
        tmp_val = np.nan
        tmp_dt = np.nan

    bp_times.append(t)
    sbp_aligned.append(sbp_val)
    dbp_aligned.append(dbp_val)
    temp_aligned.append(tmp_val)
    temp_dt_min.append(tmp_dt)

pp = np.array(sbp_aligned, dtype=float) - np.array(dbp_aligned, dtype=float)
map_arr = (np.array(sbp_aligned, dtype=float) + 2.0 * np.array(dbp_aligned, dtype=float)) / 3.0
temp_arr = np.array(temp_aligned, dtype=float)

n_bp_pairs = int(len(pp))

# --- clustering: low MAP with narrow pulse pressure ---
LOW_MAP = 65.0
# define narrow PP as ≤30 mmHg, a common clinical cutoff (and consistent with observed PP=27)
NARROW_PP = 30.0

if n_bp_pairs > 0:
    mask_low_map = map_arr < LOW_MAP
    mask_narrow_pp = pp <= NARROW_PP
    mask_cluster = mask_low_map & mask_narrow_pp

    n_low_map = int(np.sum(mask_low_map))
    n_narrow_pp = int(np.sum(mask_narrow_pp))
    n_cluster = int(np.sum(mask_cluster))

    pct_cluster_overall = (100.0 * n_cluster / n_bp_pairs) if n_bp_pairs else np.nan
    pct_cluster_given_low_map = (100.0 * n_cluster / n_low_map) if n_low_map else np.nan

    pp_med_cluster = float(np.nanmedian(pp[mask_cluster])) if n_cluster else np.nan
    map_med_cluster = float(np.nanmedian(map_arr[mask_cluster])) if n_cluster else np.nan

    pp_med_noncluster = float(np.nanmedian(pp[~mask_cluster])) if (n_bp_pairs - n_cluster) else np.nan
    map_med_noncluster = float(np.nanmedian(map_arr[~mask_cluster])) if (n_bp_pairs - n_cluster) else np.nan

    # effect size: difference in medians (robust), and Mann-Whitney U if both groups non-empty
    stats_out = {}
    if n_cluster > 0 and (n_bp_pairs - n_cluster) > 0:
        try:
            u_pp, p_pp = stats.mannwhitneyu(pp[mask_cluster], pp[~mask_cluster], alternative='two-sided')
        except Exception:
            u_pp, p_pp = np.nan, np.nan
        try:
            u_map, p_map = stats.mannwhitneyu(map_arr[mask_cluster], map_arr[~mask_cluster], alternative='two-sided')
        except Exception:
            u_map, p_map = np.nan, np.nan
        stats_out = {
            "pp_mannwhitney_u": float(u_pp) if np.isfinite(u_pp) else np.nan,
            "pp_mannwhitney_p": float(p_pp) if np.isfinite(p_pp) else np.nan,
            "map_mannwhitney_u": float(u_map) if np.isfinite(u_map) else np.nan,
            "map_mannwhitney_p": float(p_map) if np.isfinite(p_map) else np.nan,
        }
    else:
        stats_out = {
            "pp_mannwhitney_u": np.nan, "pp_mannwhitney_p": np.nan,
            "map_mannwhitney_u": np.nan, "map_mannwhitney_p": np.nan,
        }
else:
    mask_low_map = np.array([], dtype=bool)
    mask_narrow_pp = np.array([], dtype=bool)
    mask_cluster = np.array([], dtype=bool)
    n_low_map = n_narrow_pp = n_cluster = 0
    pct_cluster_overall = pct_cluster_given_low_map = np.nan
    pp_med_cluster = map_med_cluster = np.nan
    pp_med_noncluster = map_med_noncluster = np.nan
    stats_out = {
        "pp_mannwhitney_u": np.nan, "pp_mannwhitney_p": np.nan,
        "map_mannwhitney_u": np.nan, "map_mannwhitney_p": np.nan,
    }

# --- plot: PP vs MAP colored by temperature ---
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(7.5, 6.0))

# handle temperature coloring; if all NaN, fall back to time index coloring
if n_bp_pairs > 0 and np.all(~np.isfinite(temp_arr)):
    color_vals = np.arange(n_bp_pairs, dtype=float)
    c_label = "BP sample order (proxy for time)"
    cmap = "viridis"
else:
    color_vals = temp_arr
    c_label = "Temperature (°C)"
    cmap = "coolwarm"

sc = ax.scatter(pp, map_arr, c=color_vals, cmap=cmap, s=38, alpha=0.85, edgecolor="none")

# annotate thresholds/regions
ax.axhline(LOW_MAP, color="crimson", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.3, label="MAP 65 mmHg")
ax.axvline(NARROW_PP, color="darkorange", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.3, label="PP 30 mmHg")

# shade the "cluster risk" quadrant: low MAP + narrow PP
ax.fill_betweenx([np.nanmin(map_arr) - 5 if n_bp_pairs else 40, LOW_MAP],
                 x1=np.nanmin(pp) - 5 if n_bp_pairs else 0,
                 x2=NARROW_PP,
                 color="crimson", alpha=0.08, label="Low MAP & Narrow PP region")

content='# Assessment
85M presenting after a fall with significant baseline vulnerability (prior septic shock/aspiration pneumonitis/encephalopathy). Vitals show **borderline tachycardia (HR mean ~94, up to 110)** with **chronically low SBP (mean ~92; nadir 75)** and an **elevated shock index ~0.94**, which is concerning for **relative hypovolemia/early compensated shock** in a geriatric patient—even if MAP is reported “normal” (84.7). Oxygenation is **usually excellent (SpO2 mean 99.6%)** but has a **true low outlier to 81%** that cannot be ignored in someone with prior aspiration pneumonitis (could represent transient artifact, sleep/hypoventilation, or an aspiration event). Temperature is **consistently low-normal (35.2–36.8°C, mean 36.7)**, suggesting peripheral measurement; in this patient, **absence of fever does not reassure** against infection, and a small upward shift from baseline could be meaningful.

Working diagnosis at Iteration 0: **Fall likely related to hypotension/volume depletion or delirium**, with **high-risk occult injury** (intracranial bleed/occult fracture) and **need to rule out infection/aspiration recurrence** given history and qSOFA flagged as high risk in the provided metrics.

Key missing data (needed to resolve ambiguity using only bedside/monitor info + clinical history/exam):
- **Mental status/GCS and baseline comparison** (qSOFA includes AMS; we need actual exam: orientation, focal deficits, delirium features).
- **Orthostatic symptoms and circumstances of fall** (syncope vs mechanical; prodrome; head strike; anticoagulant/antiplatelet use—even if “no recorded meds,” must verify).
- **Timing/temporal alignment of vitals** (are hypotensive episodes concurrent with tachycardia, desaturation, or tachypnea? single transient values vs sustained).
- **Oxygen delivery context** (room air vs supplemental O2; waveform/pleth quality when SpO2 hit 81%).
- **Pain/injury exam findings** (hip pain, inability to bear weight, chest wall pain; signs of dehydration; GI bleed signs; urinary retention/infection symptoms).
- **Repeat/confirmatory BP method** (cuff size, manual confirmation, positional readings) given SBP nadir 75.
- **Respiratory exam context** (cough, witnessed aspiration, new sputum, increased work of breathing) since RR range includes up to 26.6.

# Hypotheses
1. **Orthostatic hypotension / dehydration** causing fall (supported by SBP mean ~92, nadir 75; elevated shock index 0.94).
2. **Occult infection with atypical presentation** (urosepsis/aspiration pneumonia) causing weakness/delirium and relative hypotension (history of septic shock; low-normal temps do not exclude).
3. **Aspiration event or evolving pneumonitis/pneumonia** (prior aspiration pneumonitis; SpO2 low outlier 81%—needs validation).
4. **Intracranial hemorrhage or concussion** after fall (high-risk age; need head strike/anticoagulation/AMS details).
5. **Occult fracture (hip/pelvis/ribs/vertebral)** contributing to pain, immobility, and physiologic stress (pain can drive HR ~110).
6. **Cardiac dysrhythmia / cardiogenic syncope** (no rhythm data provided; tachycardia range modest but fall mechanism unknown).
7. **Medication/toxin effect** (even if “no recorded meds,” elderly often have antihypertensives/sedatives contributing to hypotension/falls).

# Acuity Estimation
- **ESI Level**: **2** (High-risk geriatric fall + intermittent **SBP as low as 75** and **shock index 0.94**; potential occult sepsis/bleed/serious injury despite currently acceptable RR/SpO2 averages).
- **Pain Score**: **3/10** (fall in elderly often causes at least mild–moderate pain even before injuries are confirmed; no specific severe pain signal provided yet, so not assuming fracture-level pain).
- **ED Length of Stay**: **8 hours** (complex geriatric fall + need for close hemodynamic/respiratory monitoring and serial reassessment; potential admission depending on stability/mental status).
- **Reflection**: This is Iteration 0, so no prior ESI/pain/LOS estimates to revise. Current vitals-based risk (SBP nadir 75, elevated shock index, SpO2 outlier 81, low temperature baseline limiting fever sensitivity) justifies starting at **ESI 2** rather than 3, pending confirmation of whether hypotension/desaturation are sustained vs artifact and pending neurologic status.' additional_kwargs={} response_metadata={} tool_calls=[] invalid_tool_calls=[]

Your role is to select the most probative visual evidence to support the Doctor's diagnosis.

## Objective
Select images that confirm abnormalities, illustrate trends, or clearly rule out differentials.
Eliminate "normal" plots unless they definitively rule out a major concern (e.g., negative troponin trend).
Prioritize clean signals over noisy ones.

## Ranking Criteria
- **High relevance (8-10)**: Clear visualization of a key pathology (e.g., rapid desaturation, widening pulse pressure) or a critical negative finding.
- **Medium relevance (4-7)**: Supporting evidence, but perhaps noisy or redundant.
- **Low relevance (0-3)**: Normal, noisy, illegible, or redundant. (e.g., stable heart rate in a healthy-looking patient).

## Sufficiency Guidelines (`is_sufficient`)

  - You have not yet seen enough advanced analytics.
  - Critical tasks requested by the Consultant have not been done yet.
  - The calculated data contradicts your hypothesis and you need to pivot.
  - You simply need one more cycle of analysis to be sure.

You are a Medical Editor and Clinical Evidence Specialist.
Your role is to select the most probative visual evidence to support the Doctor's diagnosis.

## Objective
Select images that confirm abnormalities, illustrate trends, or clearly rule out differentials.
Eliminate "normal" plots unless they definitively rule out a major concern (e.g., negative troponin trend).
Prioritize clean signals over noisy ones.

## Ranking Criteria
- **High relevance (8-10)**: Clear visualization of a key pathology (e.g., rapid desaturation, widening pulse pressure) or a critical negative finding.
- **Medium relevance (4-7)**: Supporting evidence, but perhaps noisy or redundant.
- **Low relevance (0-3)**: Normal, noisy, illegible, or redundant. (e.g., stable heart rate in a healthy-looking patient).

## Sufficiency Guidelines (`is_sufficient`)
You must determine if the current evidence (Visuals + Calculations + Context) is sufficient to make a Final Diagnosis and Acuity Assessment.
  - OR further testing is impossible (no labs available) AND you have already explored all high-yield vitals-based analytics (rolling trends, distributions, correlations, etc.) AND the evidence is conclusive.
- **Set `False` if**:
  - You have not yet seen enough advanced analytics.
  - Critical tasks requested by the Consultant have not been done yet.
  - The calculated data contradicts your hypothesis and you need to pivot.
  - You simply need one more cycle of analysis to be sure.

You are a remote Specialist Consultant (e.g., Toxicology, Cardiology, or Critical Care).
Your role is to be the **Curbside Consult** for the Attending Physician (Doctor).

## Objective
1. **Identify Clinical Gaps**: Find confirmation bias, missed rule-outs, or life-threats ignored by the Doctor's working diagnosis and plan.
2. **Visual Evidence Is Required**: Do not just suggest a rule-out. Explicitly request plots or images to support your critique. These visuals provide the objective evidence needed to justify a change in clinical direction.
3. **Additive & Non-Redundant**: Review the Doctor's Proposed Plan. Do NOT duplicate their requests. Focus on different signal relationships, longer-term trajectories, or high-yield metrics the Doctor overlooked.
4. **Feasibility**: Ensure all requested tasks are strictly possible using the signals in "Clinical Data." Do not request labs or data not present in the record.

## Output Format (Markdown)
You must output your response in the following Markdown format. Do not use JSON.

# Critique
[Sharp clinical critique of the Doctor's plan. Highlight confirmation bias, missed 'Can't Miss' life-threats, or missing rule-outs.]

# Differential Diagnosis
[List of alternative diagnoses that MUST be considered.]
- [Diagnosis 1]
- [Diagnosis 2]

# Rule-out Tasks
[Specific metrics or plots to rule out the alternative diagnoses.]
- [Task 1]
- [Task 2]

## Clinical Guidelines
- Propose *additive* tasks (don't delete the Doctor's tasks unless dangerous).
- Do NOT request simple single-signal plots of signals already present in the "Clinical Data" list. A comprehensive vitals panel is already provided. Focus your requests on other analysis of distributions, rolling variability, correlations, phase-space, etc. focus on the most clinically relevant missing analytics.
- Generally 1-2 high-value tasks are better than 10 generic ones.
- **Avoid Duplicates**: Do not suggest tasks that duplicate existing calculated metrics (see "Calculated Metrics") unless the visualization itself is missing.
- **Temperature Analysis**: Consider that temperature values may be from different thermometers/sites based on the average/min/max values.
  - If values are consistently sub-36.5°C, consider peripheral measurement (axillary) and advise the doctor to re-evaluate fever thresholds.
  - Flag if specific rule-outs (e.g., Sepsis) are being missed because of strict adherence to "38.0°C" criteria when using a peripheral thermometer.

## Data Limitations
- **No Labs**: You CANNOT order new lab tests (e.g., WBC, Lactate, Troponin, Cultures, ABG).
- **Only Vitals**: You ONLY have access to the signals listed in "Clinical Data" (HR, RR, SpO2, BP, Temp).
- **Metric Feasibility**: Do not request metrics dependent on missing data.

## Clinical Context
85-year-old male with a past medical history of severe sepsis with septic shock, sepsis (unspecified organism), aspiration pneumonitis, metabolic encephalopathy, and disorientation; on no recorded medications. Presents with a fall. High risk for occult infection/aspiration recurrence, delirium/encephalopathy, dehydration/orthostatic hypotension, and injury/bleed after fall given age and prior critical illness. Baseline vitals suggest relatively low systolic BP (mean ~92) with occasional hypotension (SBP down to 75) and generally normal RR. Temperature range is low-normal (35.2–36.8°C), suggesting possible peripheral/axillary measurement; fever thresholds should be interpreted cautiously and rising temp from his baseline may be clinically significant.

## Triage Vitals Threshold Rationale
Thresholds are centered on this patient’s observed distributions, with conservative buffers for geriatric fall risk and prior septic shock history. SBP normal is set lower than standard adult norms due to documented low mean and frequent readings in the 80s–90s; values below 75 or symptomatic hypotension should be treated as high-risk. SpO2 is generally excellent, but prior aspiration pneumonitis warrants caution for drops below 92–95%. Temperature appears consistently low-normal, possibly reflecting axillary/peripheral measurement; therefore a relative rise above ~37.3°C or absolute ≥37.8°C should prompt evaluation for infection even if not meeting classic 38°C fever criteria.

## Clinical Data
- Heart Rate (bpm): 248 values, Range 80.0-110.0 (Mean: 94.05)
- Systolic BP (mmHg): 30 values, Range 75-152 (Mean: 92)
- Diastolic BP (mmHg): 30 values, Range 54-96 (Mean: 70)
- SpO2 (%): 209 values, Range 81.0-100.0 (Mean: 99.59)
- Respiratory Rate (brpm): 292 values, Range 11.0-26.6 (Mean: 16.02)
- Temperature (°C): 140 values, Range 35.2-36.8 (Mean: 36.70)

## Calculated Metrics
- shock_index: 0.944  (Triage Baseline)
- shock_index_interpretation: Elevated (0.94), above normal range (0.5-0.7). Early compensated shock possible, monitor closely.  (Triage Baseline)

- pulse_pressure: 23.0  (Triage Baseline)
- qsofa_score: 2  (Triage Baseline)
- qsofa_interpretation: High Risk (Score 2/3). Criteria met: SBP=90, RR=23. Associated with poor outcomes in sepsis.  (Triage Baseline)
- sirs: 1  (Triage Baseline)
- spo2_trend: {'first': np.float64(97.0), 'last': np.float64(99.0), 'min': 81.0, 'mean': 99.6, 'slope': np.float64(-0.0006), 'r_squared': np.float64(0.0), 'trend_pct': np.float64(-0.13)}  (Triage Baseline)

- triage_vital_panel: Attached  ()
- Plot an SpO2 distribution histogram focused on 85–100% (use clipped range and log-scaled counts) to show whether low values (including 81%) form a tail versus a single outlier.: None  ()
- Plot time-aligned Shock Index (HR/SBP) and Pulse Pressure over time with points colored by SBP bins (<80, 80–90, >90) and add a 10-minute rolling median line for both metrics.: None  ()
- Create an SpO2 hypoxemia episode plot marking episodes with SpO2 <92% for ≥2 consecutive readings and separately <88% for ≥2 readings; overlay HR and RR traces ±10 minutes around each episode.: None  ()

## Doctor's Assessment
# Assessment
The new visual evidence strengthens that this patient has **intermittent hypotension with persistently elevated shock index** and **generally narrow pulse pressure**, while the “hypoxemia” appears **artifactual/transient**.

**Hemodynamics**
- The SBP/DBP time series shows multiple **hypotensive periods (SBP <90)** clustered around ~01:00, ~01:35–01:45, and ~03:20–~03:55. The lowest SBPs are in the **mid-70s** (consistent with reported range **75–152**).
- During these low-SBP windows, **DBP is not profoundly low** (often ~55–70s), and **pulse pressure frequently remains narrow (~10–25 mmHg)**. Narrow PP with relatively preserved DBP suggests a **low stroke volume state** (e.g., hypovolemia/dehydration, reduced LV filling, or less likely obstructive physiology), rather than pure vasodilatory shock where DBP would often fall more dramatically.
- The shock index plot shows **repeated SI ~1.0–1.2** with peaks **~1.4–1.45** coinciding with **SBP <80** points—this is **not reassuring** in an 85-year-old and is consistent with **compensated shock physiology**.

**Respiratory**
- The SpO2 <90 concordance panel demonstrates the 81% nadir had **minimal physiologic accompaniment**: **ΔHR ~+1.8 bpm, ΔRR ~+1.1 brpm**, and it is explicitly flagged **“DROP-OUT SUSPECTED.”** This supports **monitor artifact/poor pleth** rather than true hypoxemia. No evidence (from vitals) of sustained aspiration-related hypoxemia at this time.

Working diagnosis (Iteration 2): **Fall likely precipitated by intermittent hypotension with low effective circulating volume/low stroke volume physiology (hypovolemia/orthostasis most likely),** with ongoing need to **exclude occult bleeding and occult infection** given age, prior septic shock history, and recurrent low SBP with elevated SI. Vitals do **not** currently support clinically significant hypoxemic respiratory failure/aspiration recurrence.

Key missing data (still limiting closure):
- **Clinical story of the fall** (syncope vs mechanical, prodrome, dehydration/poor intake, diarrhea/vomiting, melena/hematemesis).
- **Medication reconciliation**, especially antihypertensives, diuretics, sedatives, and **anticoagulants/antiplatelets**.
- **Mental status exam** (delirium vs baseline; focal neuro deficits) and head strike history to risk-stratify for intracranial bleed.
- **Orthostatic vitals** and **manual BP confirmation** when SBP is in the 70s–80s.
- **Focused trauma/injury exam** (hip/pelvis pain, inability to bear weight, abdominal tenderness, chest wall pain).
- Infection screen by history/exam (urinary symptoms, cough/sputum, rigors) since we cannot use labs.

# Hypotheses
1. **Hypovolemia/orthostatic hypotension** (poor intake, dehydration, diuretics if present) → fall; supported by **SBP down to 75**, **SI up to ~1.45**, **narrow PP ~10–25**.
2. **Occult hemorrhage** (GI bleed, traumatic bleed) causing low SV/compensated shock pattern (cannot rule out without history/exam; labs unavailable).
3. **Cardiogenic low stroke volume** (decompensated valvular disease, CHF, dysrhythmia episodes) contributing to hypotension/narrow PP (no rhythm strip provided).
4. **Occult infection/sepsis with atypical vitals** (still possible in elderly even without fever; but DBP pattern and lack of temp rise makes this less supported by vitals alone right now).
5. **Intracranial injury** (ICH/concussion) after fall—risk depends on head strike/anticoagulation/AMS (data missing).
6. **Occult fracture/pain-limited mobility** (hip/pelvis) as consequence of fall; may secondarily worsen hemodynamics via stress/poor intake.

# Acuity Estimation
- **ESI Level**: **2** (unchanged). Recurrent **SBP <90 with nadir ~75** and **shock index peaks ~1.4–1.45** in an elderly fall patient = high risk for decompensation/occult serious pathology.
- **Pain Score**: **3/10** (unchanged). Still no direct injury/pain localization provided; vitals do not show severe pain physiology.
- **ED Length of Stay**: **8 hours** (unchanged). Needs serial reassessment of hemodynamics, orthostatics, careful trauma and delirium evaluation, and disposition planning (likely admission/observation).
- **Reflection**: Compared with my prior assessment, the new plots **increase confidence** that (1) the SpO2 nadir was **artifact**, lowering concern for active aspiration/hypoxemia, and (2) the hypotension pattern is **real and recurrent** with **low-SV features** (narrow PP + elevated SI), which sustains **ESI 2** and supports ongoing concern for hypovolemia/bleeding/cardiac causes. No basis to downgrade acuity.

## Objective
Critique this plan. What are we missing? What else could this be?
Suggest specific "Rule-Out" requests to add to the Coder's queue.

# Critique
Your hemodynamic read (recurrent SBP dips + elevated SI + narrow PP → low SV physiology) is coherent, but it risks **prematurely anchoring on “hypovolemia/orthostasis”** without stress-testing two geriatric, can’t-miss alternatives that *also* present with **narrow PP + preserved DBP** and may not show dramatic RR/SpO₂ changes:

Your HR range (80–110) looks “benign,” but that can be a sampling artifact unless you explicitly evaluate **HR–BP coupling and abruptness** around hypotensive windows. Without that, “low SV” could be **rate/irregularity-mediated** rather than volume-mediated.

2) **Autonomic failure / baroreflex impairment** (common in frail elderly, Parkinsonism, diabetic autonomic neuropathy, post-sepsis dysautonomia) producing **episodic hypotension with relatively preserved DBP** and poor reflex compensation. This can mimic dehydration yet behaves differently: more **lability**, weaker HR response, and stronger **BP variance** signatures.

Also: your infection caution is appropriate, but don’t let “no fever” (and possibly axillary temps) reassure you. In older adults, **relative temperature rise** and **hemodynamic variability** can be the signal. You already noted this concept—what’s missing is an objective visualization that tests it.

- **Paroxysmal tachyarrhythmia / intermittent dysrhythmia-related hypotension** (short SVT/AF-RVR bursts or irregularity not captured by summary stats)
- **Autonomic dysfunction / orthostatic intolerance phenotype** (dysautonomia, post-sepsis autonomic impairment) with BP lability
- **Early/atypical sepsis physiology** with blunted fever response (trend/variability signal rather than absolute temp)
- **Obstructive physiology episodes** (e.g., dynamic LVOT obstruction, preload-sensitive states) suggested by narrow PP + lability (hard to prove without echo, but you *can* look for characteristic coupling patterns in vitals)

- **Early/atypical sepsis physiology** with blunted fever response (trend/variability signal rather than absolute temp)
- **Obstructive physiology episodes** (e.g., dynamic LVOT obstruction, preload-sensitive states) suggested by narrow PP + lability (hard to prove without echo, but you *can* look for characteristic coupling patterns in vitals)

- **HR–SBP coupling / lag analysis around hypotension (arrhythmia vs volume)**

The Coder accepts simple text instructions (e.g., "Calculate Shock Index", "Plot HR vs Time").

content='# Assessment
80M with major cardiopulmonary reserve limitations (CAD s/p CABG, aortic stenosis, HFpEF, prior sepsis/AKI, OSA) presenting with **true fever** (Tmax **39.1°C**, mean **38.1°C**) plus **tachycardia** (HR range **67–120**, mean **94** with current concern for HR ~**110–120**) and **relative hypotension** (SBP range **72–122**, mean **87**; triage SBP cited **81**) with **MAP ~63 mmHg** and **shock index 1.21**. RR is elevated (range **13.5–28**, mean **22**; triage RR **26**) and SpO2 is low-normal (range **92–98**, mean **95**).

Given the combination of fever + tachycardia + hypotension/MAP <65 + qSOFA **2** (SBP 81, RR 26), the working syndrome is **suspected sepsis with early septic shock physiology / high-risk sepsis**, with high likelihood of impending deterioration, and elevated risk of **demand ischemia/arrhythmia** in the setting of CAD/aortic stenosis.

**Key missing data (needed to localize source and assess perfusion severity, but not labs):**
- Clinical source clues: respiratory symptoms, dysuria/flank pain, abdominal pain/diarrhea, skin/soft tissue findings, indwelling devices, sick contacts.
- Mental status trajectory (qSOFA third criterion not addressed): baseline vs current confusion, GCS.
- Urine output / last void (bedside perfusion surrogate given no labs).
- Medication exposures (beta blockers, diuretics, vasodilators), and whether baseline SBP ~80s is truly chronic.
- Physical exam targets: lung exam, focal neuro, skin exam, volume status (JVP, edema), cardiac auscultation (AS severity clues).
- Timing: onset of fever, highest recorded temp and method, antipyretic use.
- Rhythm information (sinus vs AF/RVR) since HR variability exists and cardiac history is high risk.

# Hypotheses
1. **Sepsis (high risk) with early shock physiology** — most consistent with fever (39.1°C), hypotension (SBP 81; MAP 63), tachycardia, RR 26, shock index 1.21, qSOFA 2.
   - Likely sources to consider first in an 80M: **pneumonia**, **UTI/pyelonephritis**, **biliary/intra-abdominal infection**, **skin/soft tissue**, less likely but critical: **meningitis**, **endocarditis** (esp if murmur changes/prosthetic material), **line/device infection**.
2. **Cardiogenic component / mixed shock** — HFpEF + aortic stenosis may produce low forward flow and limited ability to compensate; fever can precipitate decompensation. (Still, the prominent fever makes infection the driver until proven otherwise.)
3. **Demand ischemia / ACS equivalent triggered by infection** — cannot be confirmed without ECG/troponin (labs unavailable), but clinically important given CAD/CABG; hypotension and tachycardia increase risk.
4. **Tachyarrhythmia contributing to hypotension** (e.g., AF with RVR) — needs rhythm assessment; could worsen MAP and perfusion.
5. **Noninfectious hyperthermic/inflammatory etiologies** (drug fever, gout flare, autoimmune) — less likely given shock physiology, but on the list if no infectious source emerges.

# Acuity Estimation
- **ESI Level**: **2** (High risk: MAP **63** <65, shock index **1.21**, qSOFA **2**, elderly with severe cardiac comorbidity; may progress to ESI 1 if persistent hypotension, altered mentation, or worsening hypoxemia requiring immediate life-saving interventions.)
- **Pain Score**: **2/10** (Fever/malaise likely; no evidence provided of severe focal pain such as stone/fracture/abdomen. Will revise if a painful source emerges.)
- **ED Length of Stay**: **8 hours** (Complex high-risk sepsis physiology in an elderly patient with significant cardiac disease—requires close monitoring, repeated reassessment, and likely admission.)
- **Reflection**: This is Iteration 0, so no prior estimates to revise. The current vitals-based metrics (shock index **1.21**, MAP **63**, qSOFA **2**, Tmax **39.1°C**) justify starting at **ESI 2** rather than 3, despite SpO2 being relatively preserved (92–98). Review of the plots refines the physiology:

- **MAP burden:** In the HR–MAP phase-space plot, **MAP <65 occurs in 45/100 aligned points (45%)**, showing **sustained borderline/low perfusion pressure**, not a single transient reading. - **Tachycardia burden:** The same plot shows **HR >110 in 0%** of aligned points. This suggests the **shock index elevation** may be driven more by **low SBP/MAP** than persistent marked tachycardia.
- **Blood pressure trend:** SBP appears **persistently low (~75–85)** earlier with later improvement toward **~90+ and up to ~120** (though BP sampling is sparse). This could reflect partial response to interventions/fluids/antipyretics or simply measurement variability.
- **HR–MAP coupling:** The rolling HR–MAP correlation plot is essentially non-informative (flat/empty), likely due to insufficient overlapping data density/coverage for that windowing approach—so we cannot conclude an inverse coupling pattern from that figure.

Your interpretation (mixed distributive + low-output/preload dependence) is plausible, but there’s a major **confirmation-bias trap**: **narrow pulse pressure + low MAP** in an 80M with **known aortic stenosis** can also reflect **fixed outflow obstruction with inadequate chronotropic compensation** (e.g., conduction disease, AF with slow ventricular response, beta-blockade—unknown here) or **measurement artifact** (oscillometric error at low pressures/irregular rhythms). You’re implicitly treating the BP numbers as fully reliable and the physiology as septic-first; the vitals you already have can be used to stress-test that assumption.

Two “can’t miss” alternatives that your current analytics don’t really adjudicate:
1) **Occult arrhythmia/conduction-related low output**: Your own summary says HR>110 is 0% on aligned data, yet raw HR range hits 120 and HR volatility is notable. If BP is being sampled intermittently, you can miss short episodes where **MAP collapses during tachyarrhythmia or bradyarrhythmia**. The absence of sustained tachycardia during hypotension could be **autonomic failure, meds, or rhythm problems**, not just “mixed shock.”
2) **Respiratory-driven hemodynamic compromise / OSA-related events**: RR is elevated with only mild SpO₂ derangements. In an older patient with OSA, **episodic hypoventilation/apnea** can produce **cyclic hypoxemia + sympathetic surges** and BP variability. Your RR–SpO₂ scatter helps, but it doesn’t test for *cyclicity* or *lagged coupling* (desaturation often lags ventilatory change).

Also: temperature looks “true fever,” but **timing** matters—if hypotension clusters *after* defervescence/antipyretics, that could argue **drug effect/vasodilation** or evolving shock rather than infection severity alone. Right now, you don’t have a **time-lag framework** across Temp → HR/RR → MAP/PP.

# Differential Diagnosis
- **Arrhythmia/conduction disease causing intermittent low cardiac output** (paroxysmal AF/flutter, SVT bursts, high-grade AV block/sinus pauses suggested by HR dips) with oscillometric BP unreliability during irregular rhythm
- **Critical aortic stenosis physiology / fixed stroke volume with inadequate chronotropic response** (can mimic “septic hypoperfusion” pattern)
- **Respiratory-event–linked instability** (OSA-related cyclic hypoxemia with sympathetic surges; early pneumonia/atelectasis with increased work of breathing out of proportion to SpO₂)
- **Medication/iatrogenic vasodilation effect** temporally linked to defervescence (antipyretics) or other administered agents (not in data—but vitals can show signature timing)

# Rule-out Tasks
- **Lagged coupling analysis (Temp → MAP/PP and Temp → HR):**  
  Create *time-aligned cross-correlation plots* (or lagged Pearson r over lags ±60 min, using nearest-neighbor alignment) for:
  - Temp vs MAP  
  - Temp vs Pulse Pressure  
  - Temp vs HR  
  Then **annotate the lag where correlation is strongest** and whether hypotension/narrow PP clusters **during rising fever** (sepsis physiology) vs **after Temp falls** (post-antipyretic vasodilation or evolving shock). This directly challenges the “fever = driver” assumption using only existing vitals.

- **Cycle/instability detection to screen for episodic rhythm/OSA patterns:**  
  Using the existing HR, RR, SpO₂ time series, generate:
  1) **Autocorrelation / power spectral density (PSD)** of SpO₂ and HR (and optionally RR) to look for **quasi-periodic cycling** (e.g., 30–120 sec periodicity suggestive of apnea-related cycles or recurrent instability).  
  2) A **recurrence/phase plot**: ΔHR (first difference) vs HR and ΔSpO₂ vs SpO₂, with points colored by time; flag **clusters of high ΔHR or ΔSpO₂** that occur near hypotensive BP timestamps (nearest-neighbor within a window).  
  Rationale: identifies intermittent events (arrhythmia bursts or apnea-cycles) that intermittent BP sampling can miss, and avoids relying on “HR>110 burden” alone.

These two additions are high-yield because they (a) test whether fever temporally drives hemodynamic collapse, and (b) look for episodic physiology consistent with arrhythmia/OSA that could explain low MAP + narrow PP without persistent tachycardia.

You are a remote Specialist Consultant (e.g., Toxicology, Cardiology, or Critical Care).
Your role is to be the **Curbside Consult** for the Attending Physician (Doctor).

## Objective
1. **Identify Clinical Gaps**: Find confirmation bias, missed rule-outs, or life-threats ignored by the Doctor's working diagnosis and plan.
2. **Visual Evidence Is Required**: Do not just suggest a rule-out. Explicitly request plots or images to support your critique. These visuals provide the objective evidence needed to justify a change in clinical direction.
3. **Additive & Non-Redundant**: Review the Doctor's Proposed Plan. Do NOT duplicate their requests. Focus on different signal relationships, longer-term trajectories, or high-yield metrics the Doctor overlooked.
4. **Feasibility**: Ensure all requested tasks are strictly possible using the signals in "Clinical Data." Do not request labs or data not present in the record.

## Output Format (Markdown)
You must output your response in the following Markdown format. Do not use JSON.

# Critique
[Sharp clinical critique of the Doctor's plan. Highlight confirmation bias, missed 'Can't Miss' life-threats, or missing rule-outs.]

# Differential Diagnosis
[List of alternative diagnoses that MUST be considered.]
- [Diagnosis 1]
- [Diagnosis 2]

# Rule-out Tasks
[Specific metrics or plots to rule out the alternative diagnoses.]
- [Task 1]
- [Task 2]

## Clinical Guidelines
- Propose *additive* tasks (don't delete the Doctor's tasks unless dangerous).
- Do NOT request simple single-signal plots of signals already present in the "Clinical Data" list. A comprehensive vitals panel is already provided. Focus your requests on other analysis of distributions, rolling variability, correlations, phase-space, etc. focus on the most clinically relevant missing analytics.
- Generally 1-2 high-value tasks are better than 10 generic ones.
- **Avoid Duplicates**: Do not suggest tasks that duplicate existing calculated metrics (see "Calculated Metrics") unless the visualization itself is missing.
- **Temperature Analysis**: Consider that temperature values may be from different thermometers/sites based on the average/min/max values.
  - If values are consistently sub-36.5°C, consider peripheral measurement (axillary) and advise the doctor to re-evaluate fever thresholds.
  - Flag if specific rule-outs (e.g., Sepsis) are being missed because of strict adherence to "38.0°C" criteria when using a peripheral thermometer.

## Data Limitations
- **No Labs**: You CANNOT order new lab tests (e.g., WBC, Lactate, Troponin, Cultures, ABG).
- **Only Vitals**: You ONLY have access to the signals listed in "Clinical Data" (HR, RR, SpO2, BP, Temp).
- **Metric Feasibility**: Do not request metrics dependent on missing data.

Your synthesis correctly separates hypotension from desaturation physiology, but it risks **premature closure** on “sepsis vs cardiogenic/arrhythmic” without proving that the hypotension is *true hemodynamic collapse* versus **measurement artifact (NIBP error)** or a **transient dysautonomia/brady-tachy pattern** that would look very different clinically.

1) **BP artifact / spurious hypotension is not excluded.** An SBP nadir of 51 with MAP baseline 71 and rapid recovery could represent real shock—but also classic NIBP failure (cuff size/position, motion, AFib, tremor). - **Autonomic failure / neurogenic shock–like physiology** in an acute neuro process (disproportionate hypotension episodes without expected respiratory compensation)

# Rolling 2–5 minute differences (ΔSBP, ΔHR) and ΔHR vs ΔSBP quadrant scatter
# Requirements: highlight (a) ΔSBP<0 & ΔHR<=0 and (b) HR surges preceding SBP drops; add point density and color by contemporaneous shock index.

def _to_arrays(ts_vals):
    if ts_vals is None or len(ts_vals) == 0:
        return np.array([]), np.array([])
    t = np.array([x[0] for x in ts_vals], dtype=object)
    v = np.array([float(x[1]) for x in ts_vals], dtype=float)
    return t, v

def _diff_in_window(t, v, min_minutes=2.0, max_minutes=5.0):
    n = len(v)
    if n < 2:
        return {
            "t2": np.array([], dtype=object),
            "v2": np.array([], dtype=float),
            "t1": np.array([], dtype=object),
            "v1": np.array([], dtype=float),
            "dt_min": np.array([], dtype=float),
            "dv": np.array([], dtype=float),
        }
    t2_list, v2_list, t1_list, v1_list, dt_list, dv_list = [], [], [], [], [], []
    for i in range(1, n):
        # find most recent prior j s.t. dt in [min_minutes, max_minutes]
        chosen_j = None
        chosen_dt = None
        for j in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
            dt = (t[i] - t[j]).total_seconds() / 60.0
            if dt < min_minutes:
                continue
            if dt > max_minutes:
                break
            chosen_j = j
            chosen_dt = dt
            break
        if chosen_j is None:
            continue
        t2_list.append(t[i]); v2_list.append(v[i])
        t1_list.append(t[chosen_j]); v1_list.append(v[chosen_j])
        dt_list.append(chosen_dt)
        dv_list.append(v[i] - v[chosen_j])
    return {
        "t2": np.array(t2_list, dtype=object),
        "v2": np.array(v2_list, dtype=float),
        "t1": np.array(t1_list, dtype=object),
        "v1": np.array(v1_list, dtype=float),
        "dt_min": np.array(dt_list, dtype=float),
        "dv": np.array(dv_list, dtype=float),
    }

def _match_nearest_time(t_src, v_src, t_query, max_gap_minutes=5.0):
    # returns matched values and gaps; NaN if no match within max gap
    if len(t_src) == 0 or len(t_query) == 0:
        return np.full(len(t_query), np.nan), np.full(len(t_query), np.inf)
    idx = 0
    matched = np.full(len(t_query), np.nan, dtype=float)
    gaps = np.full(len(t_query), np.inf, dtype=float)
    for i, tq in enumerate(t_query):
        # advance idx while next is closer
        while idx + 1 < len(t_src) and abs((t_src[idx + 1] - tq).total_seconds()) <= abs((t_src[idx] - tq).total_seconds()):
            idx += 1
        gap = abs((t_src[idx] - tq).total_seconds()) / 60.0
        gaps[i] = gap
        if gap <= max_gap_minutes:
            matched[i] = float(v_src[idx])
    return matched, gaps

def _rolling_preceding_diff(t, v, t_anchor, lookback_minutes=5.0, max_gap_minutes=5.0):
    # For each anchor time, compute v(anchor) - median(v within (anchor-lookback, anchor])
    # If insufficient history or missing anchor match, return NaN.
    if len(t) == 0 or len(t_anchor) == 0:
        return np.full(len(t_anchor), np.nan)
    v_at_anchor, gap = _match_nearest_time(t, v, t_anchor, max_gap_minutes=max_gap_minutes)
    out = np.full(len(t_anchor), np.nan, dtype=float)
    # Create numpy object arrays for t comparisons
    for i, ta in enumerate(t_anchor):
        if not np.isfinite(v_at_anchor[i]):
            continue
        start = ta - (ta - ta)  # placeholder to keep datetime type
        start = ta - (ta - ta)  # redundant but harmless
        start = ta - (ta - ta)  # keep as datetime
        start = ta - (lookback_minutes * (ta - ta)) if False else (ta - (ta - ta))  # noop to avoid timedelta import
        # manual minutes subtraction without importing timedelta: use total seconds via datetime arithmetic is not possible directly.
        # Workaround: infer start via seconds using datetime's built-in support with numpy is not allowed; do a simple scan with dt calc.
        vals = []
        for k in range(len(t)):
            if t[k] > ta:
                break
            dtm = (ta - t[k]).total_seconds() / 60.0
            if 0.0 < dtm <= lookback_minutes:
                vals.append(v[k])
        if len(vals) < 2:
            continue
        out[i] = v_at_anchor[i] - float(np.median(np.array(vals, dtype=float)))
    return out

# Extract arrays
t_hr, v_hr = _to_arrays(heart_rate)
t_sbp, v_sbp = _to_arrays(systolic_bp)

# Compute within-series 2–5 minute deltas
sbp_d = _diff_in_window(t_sbp, v_sbp, 2.0, 5.0)
hr_d = _diff_in_window(t_hr, v_hr, 2.0, 5.0)

# Align by using SBP delta end-times (t2) as anchor, and compute ΔHR (2-5 min) nearest in time
dSBP = sbp_d["dv"]
t_anchor = sbp_d["t2"]

# Nearest HR delta to SBP anchor time
# Use HR delta "t2" times as reference, match nearest within 5 minutes
hr_delta_at_anchor, hr_delta_gap = _match_nearest_time(hr_d["t2"], hr_d["dv"], t_anchor, max_gap_minutes=5.0)

# Contemporaneous shock index at anchor time using nearest HR and SBP raw values
hr_at_anchor, hr_gap = _match_nearest_time(t_hr, v_hr, t_anchor, max_gap_minutes=5.0)
sbp_at_anchor, sbp_gap = _match_nearest_time(t_sbp, v_sbp, t_anchor, max_gap_minutes=5.0)
shock_at_anchor = hr_at_anchor / sbp_at_anchor
shock_at_anchor[~np.isfinite(shock_at_anchor)] = np.nan

# Keep rows with finite dSBP and dHR and finite shock
valid = np.isfinite(dSBP) & np.isfinite(hr_delta_at_anchor) & np.isfinite(shock_at_anchor)
dSBP_v = dSBP[valid]
dHR_v = hr_delta_at_anchor[valid]
shock_v = shock_at_anchor[valid]
t_v = t_anchor[valid]
hrgap_v = hr_delta_gap[valid]
gap_sbp_v = sbp_gap[valid]
gap_hr_v = hr_gap[valid]

# Identify quadrants of interest:
# (a) SBP drops without HR rise: ΔSBP<0 and ΔHR<=0
mask_no_comp = (dSBP_v < 0) & (dHR_v <= 0)

# (b) HR surges preceding SBP drops:
# define HR surge as +10 bpm increase from prior-5-min median at the time of SBP measurement AND ΔSBP<0
dHR_pre5 = _rolling_preceding_diff(t_hr, v_hr, t_v, lookback_minutes=5.0, max_gap_minutes=5.0)
mask_hr_surge = (dSBP_v < 0) & (dHR_pre5 >= 10.0)

# Density estimate via 2D histogram (no extra imports)
if len(dSBP_v) > 0:
    x = dSBP_v
    y = dHR_v
    # robust binning
    xb = int(np.clip(np.sqrt(len(x)) * 2, 25, 80))
    yb = int(np.clip(np.sqrt(len(y)) * 2, 25, 80))
    xedges = np.linspace(np.nanpercentile(x, 1), np.nanpercentile(x, 99), xb + 1)
    yedges = np.linspace(np.nanpercentile(y, 1), np.nanpercentile(y, 99), yb + 1)
    H, xe, ye = np.histogram2d(x, y, bins=[xedges, yedges])
    # map each point to its bin density
    xi = np.clip(np.searchsorted(xe, x, side="right") - 1, 0, H.shape[0] - 1)
    yi = np.clip(np.searchsorted(ye, y, side="right") - 1, 0, H.shape[1] - 1)
    dens = H[xi, yi].astype(float)
    # scale for alpha/size
    dens_scaled = (dens - np.nanmin(dens)) / (np.nanmax(dens) - np.nanmin(dens) + 1e-9)
else:
    dens = np.array([], dtype=float)
    dens_scaled = np.array([], dtype=float)

# Plot: background density + scatter colored by shock index; highlight two event types
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(10, 7))

# density background using hexbin (counts)
if len(dSBP_v) > 5:
    ax.hexbin(dSBP_v, dHR_v, gridsize=40, cmap="Greys", mincnt=1, linewidths=0, alpha=0.35)

# main scatter colored by shock index
sc = ax.scatter(
    dSBP_v, dHR_v,
    c=shock_v,
    cmap="viridis",
    s=18 + 42 * (dens_scaled if len(dens_scaled) else 0),
    alpha=0.75,
    edgecolors="none"
)

# quadrant lines
ax.axvline(0, color="black", linewidth=1, alpha=0.6)
ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=1, alpha=0.6)

# highlight (a): ΔSBP<0 & ΔHR<=0
if np.any(mask_no_comp):
    ax.scatter(
        dSBP_v[mask_no_comp], dHR_v[mask_no_comp],
        facecolors="none", edgecolors="red",
        s=90, linewidths=1.6,
        label="ΔSBP<0 & ΔHR≤0 (no compensatory tachy)"
    )

# highlight (b): HR surge preceding SBP drop
if np.any(mask_hr_surge):
    ax.scatter(
        dSBP_v[mask_hr_surge], dHR_v[mask_hr_surge],
        marker="^", c="orange",
        s=70, alpha=0.9,
        edgecolors="black", linewidths=0.3,
        label="HR surge ≥10 bpm vs prior-5-min median + ΔSBP<0"
    )

cbar = plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax)
cbar.set_label("Contemporaneous Shock Index (HR/SBP)")

ax.set_title("Rolling 2–5 min ΔHR vs ΔSBP (colored by shock index; density background)")
ax.set_xlabel("ΔSBP over 2–5 min (mmHg)")
ax.set_ylabel("ΔHR over 2–5 min (bpm)")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.25)
ax.legend(loc="best", frameon=True, fontsize=9)

save_plot("deltaHR_vs_deltaSBP_quadrants_density_shockindex.png", fig=fig)

# Summaries
n_total = int(len(dSBP_v))
n_no_comp = int(np.sum(mask_no_comp)) if n_total else 0
n_hr_surge = int(np.sum(mask_hr_surge)) if n_total else 0

# Shock index distribution for flagged groups
def _summ(v):
    v = v[np.isfinite(v)]
    if len(v) == 0:
        return {"n": 0, "median": np.nan, "p25": np.nan, "p75": np.nan}
    return {
        "n": int(len(v)),
        "median": float(np.median(v)),
        "p25": float(np.percentile(v, 25)),
        "p75": float(np.percentile(v, 75)),
    }

result = {
    "patient_context": {"age": age, "gender": gender},
    "deltas_window_minutes": {"min": 2.0, "max": 5.0},
    "alignment": {
        "anchor": "SBP delta end-time (t2)",
        "hr_delta_matched_to_anchor": {"max_gap_minutes": 5.0, "median_gap_minutes": float(np.nanmedian(hrgap_v)) if len(hrgap_v) else np.nan},
        "shock_index_components_matched_to_anchor": {
            "max_gap_minutes": 5.0,
            "median_hr_gap_minutes": float(np.nanmedian(gap_hr_v)) if len(gap_hr_v) else np.nan,
            "median_sbp_gap_minutes": float(np.nanmedian(gap_sbp_v)) if len(gap_sbp_v) else np.nan,
        },
    },
    "counts": {
        "n_pairs_total": n_total,
        "n_no_compensatory_response": n_no_comp,
        "n_hr_surge_preceding_sbp_drop": n_hr_surge,
    },
    "thresholds": {
        "no_comp_response": {"dSBP": "<0 mmHg", "dHR": "≤0 bpm"},
        "hr_surge_preceding_sbp_drop": {"dSBP": "<0 mmHg", "HR_vs_prior_5min_median": "≥+10 bpm"},
    },
    "distributions": {
        "dSBP_mmHg": _summ(dSBP_v),
        "dHR_bpm": _summ(dHR_v),
        "shock_index_at_anchor": _summ(shock_v),
        "shock_index_no_comp": _summ(shock_v[mask_no_comp] if n_total else np.array([])),
        "shock_index_hr_surge": _summ(shock_v[mask_hr_surge] if n_total else np.array([])),
    },

        "shock_index_interpretation": shock_index_interpretation,
        "map_value": float(map_value),
        "map_interpretation": map_interpretation,

        "qsofa_interpretation": qsofa_interpretation,

)

# Combined time-aligned HR/SBP (+MAP if available), hypotension annotations, and HR–SBP cross-correlation by segment
# Required outputs: result, interpretation

# ---- Helpers ----
def _to_arrays(ts_list):
    if ts_list is None or len(ts_list) == 0:
        return np.array([]), np.array([])
    t = np.array([x[0] for x in ts_list], dtype=object)
    v = np.array([float(x[1]) for x in ts_list], dtype=float)
    return t, v

def _nearest_interp(t_src, v_src, t_grid):
    # nearest-neighbor with monotone pointers (O(n+m)); returns np.nan where no source
    n = len(t_src)
    if n == 0 or len(t_grid) == 0:
        return np.full(len(t_grid), np.nan, dtype=float)
    t_src_py = list(t_src)
    v_out = np.full(len(t_grid), np.nan, dtype=float)
    j = 0
    for i, tg in enumerate(t_grid):
        # advance j to last <= tg
        while j + 1 < n and t_src_py[j + 1] <= tg:
            j += 1
        # choose between j and j+1
        if t_src_py[j] > tg:
            # tg before first
            cand_j = 0
            v_out[i] = v_src[cand_j]
        elif j + 1 < n:
            dt0 = abs((tg - t_src_py[j]).total_seconds())
            dt1 = abs((t_src_py[j + 1] - tg).total_seconds())
            v_out[i] = v_src[j] if dt0 <= dt1 else v_src[j + 1]
        else:
            v_out[i] = v_src[j]
    return v_out

def _resample_to_grid(t_src, v_src, t0, t1, step_seconds=30):
    if len(t_src) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=object), np.array([], dtype=float)
    # Build grid
    total_sec = (t1 - t0).total_seconds()
    if total_sec <= 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=object), np.array([], dtype=float)
    n_steps = int(np.floor(total_sec / step_seconds)) + 1
    grid = np.array([t0 + (k * np.timedelta64(step_seconds, 's')).astype('timedelta64[s]').astype(object)
                     for k in range(n_steps)], dtype=object)
    vals = _nearest_interp(t_src, v_src, grid)
    return grid, vals

def _rolling_median(x, window_n):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return x
    w = int(max(1, window_n))
    out = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype=float)
    for i in range(n):
        a = max(0, i - w + 1)
        seg = x[a:i + 1]
        seg = seg[np.isfinite(seg)]
        out[i] = np.nan if seg.size == 0 else float(np.median(seg))
    return out

def _find_hypotensive_windows(t_sbp, sbp_vals, threshold=90.0, gap_merge_seconds=120):
    # Returns list of (start, end) windows where sbp<threshold, merging short gaps
    if len(t_sbp) == 0:
        return []
    is_hypo = np.isfinite(sbp_vals) & (sbp_vals < threshold)
    windows = []
    start = None
    last_t = None
    for t, flag in zip(t_sbp, is_hypo):
        if flag and start is None:
            start = t
            last_t = t
        elif flag and start is not None:
            last_t = t
        elif (not flag) and start is not None:
            windows.append((start, last_t))
            start = None
            last_t = None
    if start is not None:
        windows.append((start, last_t))

    if not windows:
        return []

    # merge windows separated by small gaps
    merged = [windows[0]]
    for s, e in windows[1:]:
        ps, pe = merged[-1]
        gap = (s - pe).total_seconds()
        if gap <= gap_merge_seconds:
            merged[-1] = (ps, e)
        else:
            merged.append((s, e))
    return merged

def _mask_from_windows(t_grid, windows):
    if len(t_grid) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=bool)
    mask = np.zeros(len(t_grid), dtype=bool)
    if not windows:
        return mask
    for (s, e) in windows:
        for i, tg in enumerate(t_grid):
            if tg < s:
                continue
            if tg > e:
                # since grid is sorted, can break for this window
                pass
        # vectorized compare using list comprehension due to dtype=object
        mask |= np.array([(tg >= s and tg <= e) for tg in t_grid], dtype=bool)
    return mask

def _corr_by_lags(hr_x, sbp_y, max_lag_steps):
    # correlation at each integer lag where sbp is shifted relative to hr:
    # lag>0: sbp occurs later (sbp[t+lag] with hr[t]) -> hr leads sbp by lag
    hr_x = np.asarray(hr_x, dtype=float)
    sbp_y = np.asarray(sbp_y, dtype=float)
    lags = np.arange(-max_lag_steps, max_lag_steps + 1, dtype=int)
    r = np.full(len(lags), np.nan, dtype=float)

    for k, lag in enumerate(lags):
        if lag < 0:
            x = hr_x[-lag:]
            y = sbp_y[:len(sbp_y) + lag]
        elif lag > 0:
            x = hr_x[:len(hr_x) - lag]
            y = sbp_y[lag:]
        else:
            x = hr_x
            y = sbp_y

        valid = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
        if valid.sum() >= 10:
            xv = x[valid]
            yv = y[valid]
            sx = np.std(xv)
            sy = np.std(yv)
            if sx > 0 and sy > 0:
                r[k] = float(np.corrcoef(xv, yv)[0, 1])
    return lags, r

# ---- Extract time series ----
t_hr, v_hr = _to_arrays(heart_rate)
t_sbp, v_sbp = _to_arrays(systolic_bp)
t_dbp, v_dbp = _to_arrays(diastolic_bp)

# Determine overlap window for alignment
all_t = []
if len(t_hr) > 0:
    all_t += [t_hr[0], t_hr[-1]]
if len(t_sbp) > 0:
    all_t += [t_sbp[0], t_sbp[-1]]
if len(all_t) == 0:
    result = {
        "status": "no_data",
        "hypotension_windows": [],
        "cross_correlation": {"lags_minutes": [], "hypotensive": [], "non_hypotensive": []}
    }
    interpretation = "Insufficient data to plot aligned HR/SBP or compute cross-correlation."
else:
    t0 = min(all_t)
    t1 = max(all_t)

    # Compute MAP series (if SBP/DBP available)
    have_map_series = (len(t_sbp) > 0 and len(t_dbp) > 0)

    # Align SBP onto DBP timestamps to compute MAP at DBP times
    if have_map_series:
        sbp_at_dbp = _nearest_interp(t_sbp, v_sbp, t_dbp)
        map_vals = (sbp_at_dbp + 2.0 * v_dbp) / 3.0
        t_map = t_dbp
    else:
        t_map = np.array([], dtype=object)
        map_vals = np.array([], dtype=float)

    # Resample to a common grid for cross-correlation
    step_seconds = 30  # supports ±5 min lags as integer steps (10 steps per 5 min)
    t_grid, hr_grid = _resample_to_grid(t_hr, v_hr, t0, t1, step_seconds=step_seconds)
    _, sbp_grid = _resample_to_grid(t_sbp, v_sbp, t0, t1, step_seconds=step_seconds)
    _, map_grid = _resample_to_grid(t_map, map_vals, t0, t1, step_seconds=step_seconds) if have_map_series else (t_grid, np.full(len(t_grid), np.nan))

    # Hypotensive windows from native SBP series and mapped onto grid
    hypo_windows = _find_hypotensive_windows(t_sbp, v_sbp, threshold=90.0, gap_merge_seconds=120)
    hypo_mask = _mask_from_windows(t_grid, hypo_windows)
    non_mask = ~hypo_mask

    # Cross-correlation by segment (compute on masked segments; remove gaps via finite mask)
    max_lag_minutes = 5
    max_lag_steps = int((max_lag_minutes * 60) // step_seconds)

    # For stability, create segmented arrays with NaNs outside segment and then compute correlations using valid points
    hr_hypo = hr_grid.copy()
    sbp_hypo = sbp_grid.copy()
    hr_hypo[~hypo_mask] = np.nan
    sbp_hypo[~hypo_mask] = np.nan

    hr_non = hr_grid.copy()
    sbp_non = sbp_grid.copy()
    hr_non[~non_mask] = np.nan
    sbp_non[~non_mask] = np.nan

    lags_steps, r_hypo = _corr_by_lags(hr_hypo, sbp_hypo, max_lag_steps=max_lag_steps)
    _, r_non = _corr_by_lags(hr_non, sbp_non, max_lag_steps=max_lag_steps)
    lags_minutes = lags_steps * (step_seconds / 60.0)

    # Rolling median (10-minute) for display
    window_n = int(round((10 * 60) / step_seconds))
    hr_med = _rolling_median(hr_grid, window_n)
    sbp_med = _rolling_median(sbp_grid, window_n)
    map_med = _rolling_median(map_grid, window_n) if have_map_series else None

    # ---- Plot combined figure ----
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, sharex=True, figsize=(12, 8), constrained_layout=True)

    # Panel 1: Time-aligned traces with hypotension shading
    ax = axes[0]
    if len(t_grid) > 0:
        ax.plot(t_grid, hr_grid, color="#1f77b4", alpha=0.35, linewidth=1.0, label="HR (bpm)")
        ax.plot(t_grid, hr_med, color="#1f77b4", linewidth=2.0, label="HR 10-min rolling median")

        ax2 = ax.twinx()
        ax2.plot(t_grid, sbp_grid, color="#d62728", alpha=0.35, linewidth=1.0, label="SBP (mmHg)")
        ax2.plot(t_grid, sbp_med, color="#d62728", linewidth=2.0, label="SBP 10-min rolling median")
        ax2.axhline(90.0, color="#d62728", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.7)

        if have_map_series:
            ax2.plot(t_grid, map_grid, color="#2ca02c", alpha=0.25, linewidth=1.0, label="Derived MAP (mmHg)")

        ax2.set_ylabel("SBP / MAP (mmHg)")
        ax.set_title("Time-aligned HR and SBP (and derived MAP if available); hypotension windows shaded (SBP<90 mmHg)")

        h2, l2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
        ax2.legend(h1 + h2, l1 + l2, loc="upper right", frameon=True, fontsize=9)
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.2)

    # Panel 2: Cross-correlation
    axc = axes[1]
    axc.plot(lags_minutes, r_non, color="#7f7f7f", linewidth=2.0, label="Non-hypotensive (SBP≥90)")
    axc.plot(lags_minutes, r_hypo, color="#d62728", linewidth=2.0, label="Hypotensive (SBP<90)")
    axc.axhline(0.0, color="black", linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.5)
    axc.axvline(0.0, color="black", linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.5)
    axc.set_xlim([-max_lag_minutes, max_lag_minutes])
    axc.set_xlabel("Lag (minutes)   [positive = HR leads SBP]")
    axc.set_ylabel("Pearson r (HR vs SBP)")
    axc.set_title("HR–SBP cross-correlation by segment (lags −5 to +5 minutes)")
    axc.grid(True, alpha=0.2)
    axc.legend(loc="best", frameon=True, fontsize=9)

    # ---- Summaries for result/interpretation ----
    def _count_minutes(mask):
        if mask.size == 0:
            return 0.0
        return float(mask.sum() * (step_seconds / 60.0))

    hypo_minutes = _count_minutes(hypo_mask)
    total_minutes = float(len(t_grid) * (step_seconds / 60.0)) if len(t_grid) > 0 else 0.0

    peak_lag_non, peak_r_non = _peak_corr(lags_minutes, r_non)

        "hypotension": {
            "threshold_sbp_mmHg": 90.0,
            "n_windows": int(len(hypo_windows)),
            "total_hypotensive_minutes_on_grid": hypo_minutes,
            "total_minutes_on_grid": total_minutes,
            "hypotensive_fraction": hypo_fraction,
            "windows": [(w[0], w[1]) for w in hypo_windows],

# Align BP (pulse pressure) to nearest temperature within a window, then compute lagged cross-correlation
# and highlight lag distribution for narrow PP episodes (PP<=30).

# --- helpers (no imports) ---
def _to_arrays(ts_vals):
    t = [tv[0] for tv in ts_vals]
    v = [float(tv[1]) for tv in ts_vals]
    return t, np.asarray(v, dtype=float)

def _nearest_within_window(target_times, source_times, source_values, window_min=30.0):
    # For each target time, find nearest source time; accept only if within window.
    n_src = len(source_times)
    if n_src == 0:
        return np.full(len(target_times), np.nan), np.full(len(target_times), np.nan)
    out_vals = np.full(len(target_times), np.nan)
    out_dt_min = np.full(len(target_times), np.nan)
    j = 0
    for i, tt in enumerate(target_times):
        while j + 1 < n_src and source_times[j + 1] <= tt:
            j += 1
        best_j = j
        best_abs = abs((source_times[best_j] - tt).total_seconds()) / 60.0
        if j + 1 < n_src:
            cand_abs = abs((source_times[j + 1] - tt).total_seconds()) / 60.0
            if cand_abs < best_abs:
                best_j = j + 1
                best_abs = cand_abs
        if best_abs <= window_min:
            out_vals[i] = float(source_values[best_j])
            out_dt_min[i] = float((source_times[best_j] - tt).total_seconds() / 60.0)  # + means temp after BP
    return out_vals, out_dt_min

def _lagged_corr(x, y, lag_steps):
    # Pearson correlation of x vs shifted y: corr(x[t], y[t+lag])
    # lag>0 means y leads x by lag steps; lag<0 means x leads y.
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    n = len(x)
    r = np.full(len(lag_steps), np.nan, dtype=float)
    for k, lag in enumerate(lag_steps):
        if lag == 0:
            xs, ys = x, y
        elif lag > 0:
            if lag >= n:
                continue
            xs, ys = x[:-lag], y[lag:]
        else:
            L = -lag
            if L >= n:
                continue
            xs, ys = x[L:], y[:-L]
        m = np.isfinite(xs) & np.isfinite(ys)
        if m.sum() >= 5:
            xs2 = xs[m]
            ys2 = ys[m]
            if np.std(xs2) > 0 and np.std(ys2) > 0:
                r[k] = np.corrcoef(xs2, ys2)[0, 1]
    return r

# --- compute pulse pressure at BP samples ---
sbp_t, sbp_v = _to_arrays(systolic_bp)
dbp_t, dbp_v = _to_arrays(diastolic_bp)

# Use nearest DBP within a small window of SBP to compute PP at SBP times (avoids assuming alignment).
dbp_near_v, dbp_near_dt = _nearest_within_window(sbp_t, dbp_t, dbp_v, window_min=5.0)
pp_v = sbp_v - dbp_near_v
pp_t = np.asarray(sbp_t, dtype=object)

valid_pp = np.isfinite(pp_v)
pp_t = pp_t[valid_pp]
pp_v = pp_v[valid_pp]

# --- align temperature to BP times using nearest-neighbor within window ---
temp_t, temp_v = _to_arrays(temperature)
temp_at_bp, temp_dt_min = _nearest_within_window(pp_t.tolist(), temp_t, temp_v, window_min=30.0)

m_pair = np.isfinite(pp_v) & np.isfinite(temp_at_bp)
pp_t2 = pp_t[m_pair]
pp2 = pp_v[m_pair]
temp2 = temp_at_bp[m_pair]
temp_dt2 = temp_dt_min[m_pair]  # + means temp after BP at that pairing

# If too few pairs, still produce outputs gracefully.
# --- resample to uniform 1-min grid for lagged correlation ---
if len(pp_t2) >= 6:
    t0 = pp_t2[0]
    minutes = np.array([(t - t0).total_seconds() / 60.0 for t in pp_t2], dtype=float)
    t_end = minutes.max()
    grid = np.arange(0.0, t_end + 1.0, 1.0, dtype=float)

    # interpolate PP and Temp onto grid (linear); protect monotonicity
    order = np.argsort(minutes)
    minutes_s = minutes[order]
    pp_s = pp2[order]
    temp_s = temp2[order]

    # Remove any duplicate time points for interpolation stability
    uniq_t, uniq_idx = np.unique(minutes_s, return_index=True)
    pp_u = pp_s[uniq_idx]
    temp_u = temp_s[uniq_idx]

    # Interpolate; outside range -> nan
    pp_g = np.interp(grid, uniq_t, pp_u, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)
    temp_g = np.interp(grid, uniq_t, temp_u, left=np.nan, right=np.nan)

    # Mask to overlapping finite samples
    finite_g = np.isfinite(pp_g) & np.isfinite(temp_g)
    # Keep full arrays for shifting; correlation function will mask
    lag_steps = np.arange(-60, 61, 1, dtype=int)
    r_lags = _lagged_corr(pp_g, temp_g, lag_steps)

    # Peak correlation by absolute magnitude
    finite_r = np.isfinite(r_lags)
    if finite_r.any():
        peak_idx = np.nanargmax(np.abs(r_lags))
        peak_lag_min = int(lag_steps[peak_idx])
        peak_r = float(r_lags[peak_idx])
    else:
        peak_idx = None
        peak_lag_min = None
        peak_r = np.nan
else:
    lag_steps = np.arange(-60, 61, 1, dtype=int)
    r_lags = np.full(len(lag_steps), np.nan)
    peak_idx = None
    peak_lag_min = None
    peak_r = np.nan
    grid = np.array([])
    pp_g = np.array([])
    temp_g = np.array([])

# --- lag distribution for narrow PP episodes (PP<=30) ---
pp_narrow_mask = np.isfinite(pp2) & (pp2 <= 30.0) & np.isfinite(temp_dt2)
narrow_lags = temp_dt2[pp_narrow_mask]  # minutes (temp time - bp time)
# Also provide overall pairing lag distribution as context
all_lags = temp_dt2[np.isfinite(temp_dt2)]

# --- plot: lagged cross-correlation and lag distribution histogram for narrow PP ---
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 8), constrained_layout=True)

# Cross-correlation plot
ax = axes[0]
ax.axhline(0, color="0.7", lw=1)
ax.plot(lag_steps, r_lags, color="tab:blue", lw=2)
ax.set_xlim(-60, 60)
ax.set_xlabel("Lag (min)  [positive: Temp leads PP; negative: Temp lags PP]")
ax.set_ylabel("Pearson r")
ax.set_title("Lagged cross-correlation: Temperature vs Pulse Pressure (nearest-neighbor aligned)")

if peak_lag_min is not None and np.isfinite(peak_r):
    ax.axvline(peak_lag_min, color="tab:red", lw=2, alpha=0.8)
    ax.scatter([peak_lag_min], [peak_r], color="tab:red", zorder=5)
    ax.annotate(f"peak |r|={abs(peak_r):.3f}\nr={peak_r:.3f}\nlag={peak_lag_min:+d} min",
                xy=(peak_lag_min, peak_r),
                xytext=(peak_lag_min + (5 if peak_lag_min < 30 else -25), peak_r + (0.1 if peak_r < 0.6 else -0.2)),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="tab:red", lw=1),
                fontsize=10)

# Lag distribution plot (pairing offsets)
ax2 = axes[1]
bins = np.arange(-30, 31, 2, dtype=float)
if len(all_lags) > 0:
    ax2.hist(all_lags, bins=bins, alpha=0.35, color="0.5", label="All BP–Temp pair lags")
if len(narrow_lags) > 0:

ax2.set_xlim(-30, 30)
ax2.set_xlabel("Pairing lag = (Temp time − BP time), minutes")
ax2.set_ylabel("Count")
ax2.set_title("Nearest-neighbor BP–Temp pairing lag distribution (highlight: narrow pulse pressure)")
ax2.legend(loc="best", frameon=False)

save_plot("temp_pp_lagged_xcorr_and_narrow_pp_lags.png", fig=fig)

# --- outputs ---
# Compute burden of narrow PP among aligned pairs
n_pairs = int(len(pp2))
n_narrow = int(np.sum(np.isfinite(pp2) & (pp2 <= 30.0)))
pct_narrow = (100.0 * n_narrow / n_pairs) if n_pairs > 0 else np.nan

# Summarize lag distribution for narrow PP episodes
if len(narrow_lags) > 0:
    lag_med = float(np.nanmedian(narrow_lags))

        "bp_temp_aligned_pairs": n_pairs,
        "temp_window_min": 30.0,

# Lagged cross-correlation between Temperature and MAP (nearest-neighbor aligned pairs)
# Required outputs: result, interpretation

# ---- helpers ----
def _extract_xy(ts):
    if ts is None or len(ts) == 0:
        return np.array([]), np.array([])
    t = np.array([p[0] for p in ts], dtype=object)
    v = np.array([float(p[1]) for p in ts], dtype=float)
    return t, v

def _nn_align(base_times, query_times, query_vals, max_abs_minutes):
    """
    For each time in base_times, pick nearest query_time and return aligned query_vals.
    Keep only matches within max_abs_minutes.
    """
    if len(base_times) == 0 or len(query_times) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=int), np.array([], dtype=int), np.array([], dtype=float), np.array([], dtype=float)
    bt = np.array([dt.timestamp() for dt in base_times], dtype=float)
    qt = np.array([dt.timestamp() for dt in query_times], dtype=float)

    idx_base = []
    idx_query = []
    dmins = []

    # query_times are chronological; use searchsorted for nearest neighbor
    for i, tsec in enumerate(bt):
        j = int(np.searchsorted(qt, tsec))
        cand = []
        if 0 <= j < len(qt):
            cand.append(j)
        if 0 <= j - 1 < len(qt):
            cand.append(j - 1)
        if len(cand) == 0:
            continue
        # choose nearest absolute time delta
        best_j = min(cand, key=lambda k: abs(qt[k] - tsec))
        dm = abs(qt[best_j] - tsec) / 60.0
        if dm <= max_abs_minutes:
            idx_base.append(i)
            idx_query.append(best_j)
            dmins.append(dm)

    if len(idx_base) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=int), np.array([], dtype=int), np.array([], dtype=float), np.array([], dtype=float)

    idx_base = np.array(idx_base, dtype=int)
    idx_query = np.array(idx_query, dtype=int)
    dmins = np.array(dmins, dtype=float)
    return idx_base, idx_query, dmins, query_vals[idx_query]

def _pearsonr_safe(x, y):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    m = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    x = x[m]
    y = y[m]
    if len(x) < 3:
        return np.nan, np.nan, int(len(x))
    if np.std(x) == 0 or np.std(y) == 0:
        return np.nan, np.nan, int(len(x))
    r, p = stats.pearsonr(x, y)
    return float(r), float(p), int(len(x))

def _map_from_bp(sbp_list, dbp_list, max_abs_minutes=5.0):
    st, sv = _extract_xy(sbp_list)
    dt, dv = _extract_xy(dbp_list)
    if len(st) == 0 or len(dt) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=object), np.array([], dtype=float)

    # align DBP to SBP timestamps to compute MAP at SBP times
    idx_s, idx_d, dmins, aligned_dbp = _nn_align(st, dt, dv, max_abs_minutes=max_abs_minutes)
    if len(idx_s) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=object), np.array([], dtype=float)

    sbp_al = sv[idx_s]
    dbp_al = aligned_dbp
    map_al = (sbp_al + 2.0 * dbp_al) / 3.0
    times_al = st[idx_s]
    return times_al, map_al

def _temp_slope_at_map_times(map_times, temp_times, temp_vals, window_minutes=20.0):
    """Estimate local temperature slope (°C/min) around each map_time using a local linear fit in a window."""
    if len(map_times) == 0 or len(temp_times) == 0:
        return np.array([], dtype=float), np.array([], dtype=int)

    mt = np.array([dt.timestamp() for dt in map_times], dtype=float)
    tt = np.array([dt.timestamp() for dt in temp_times], dtype=float)
    tv = np.asarray(temp_vals, dtype=float)

    slopes = np.full(len(map_times), np.nan, dtype=float)
    ns = np.zeros(len(map_times), dtype=int)

    halfwin = window_minutes * 60.0
    for i, tsec in enumerate(mt):
        m = np.abs(tt - tsec) <= halfwin
        n = int(np.sum(m))
        ns[i] = n
        if n < 3:
            continue
        x = (tt[m] - tsec) / 60.0  # minutes relative
        y = tv[m]
        # linear regression slope y = a + b*x
        # Use np.polyfit with degree 1
        try:
            b = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)[0]
            slopes[i] = float(b)  # °C per minute
        except Exception:
            slopes[i] = np.nan
    return slopes, ns

# ---- build MAP series (nearest-neighbor SBP/DBP aligned) ----
map_times, map_series = _map_from_bp(systolic_bp, diastolic_bp, max_abs_minutes=5.0)

# ---- build Temperature series ----
temp_times, temp_vals = _extract_xy(temperature)

# ---- compute lagged cross-correlation using nearest-neighbor alignment at each lag ----
lags = np.arange(-60, 61, 1, dtype=int)  # minutes
r_vals = np.full_like(lags, np.nan, dtype=float)
p_vals = np.full_like(lags, np.nan, dtype=float)
n_pairs = np.zeros_like(lags, dtype=int)

max_match_minutes = 5.0  # allowed NN match between lagged MAP time and Temp time

if len(map_times) > 0 and len(temp_times) > 0:
    mt_sec = np.array([dt.timestamp() for dt in map_times], dtype=float)
    tt_sec = np.array([dt.timestamp() for dt in temp_times], dtype=float)

    # For nearest neighbor, use sorted temp times; already chronological but enforce sort
    order_t = np.argsort(tt_sec)
    tt_sec = tt_sec[order_t]
    tv = temp_vals[order_t]

    for k, lag in enumerate(lags):
        shifted_mt_sec = mt_sec + lag * 60.0  # correlate Temp(t) with MAP(t+lag)
        # find nearest temp for each shifted MAP time
        idx_temp = []
        idx_map = []
        for i, tsec in enumerate(shifted_mt_sec):
            j = int(np.searchsorted(tt_sec, tsec))
            cand = []
            if 0 <= j < len(tt_sec):
                cand.append(j)
            if 0 <= j - 1 < len(tt_sec):
                cand.append(j - 1)
            if len(cand) == 0:
                continue
            best_j = min(cand, key=lambda q: abs(tt_sec[q] - tsec))
            dm = abs(tt_sec[best_j] - tsec) / 60.0
            if dm <= max_match_minutes:
                idx_map.append(i)
                idx_temp.append(best_j)

        if len(idx_map) < 3:
            continue

        x_temp = tv[np.array(idx_temp, dtype=int)]
        y_map = map_series[np.array(idx_map, dtype=int)]
        r, p, n = _pearsonr_safe(x_temp, y_map)
        r_vals[k] = r
        p_vals[k] = p
        n_pairs[k] = n

# peak correlation by absolute r (ignoring NaNs)
if np.all(~np.isfinite(r_vals)):
    peak_idx = None
    peak_lag = None
    peak_r = np.nan
    peak_p = np.nan
    peak_n = 0
else:
    peak_idx = int(np.nanargmax(np.abs(r_vals)))
    peak_lag = int(lags[peak_idx])
    peak_r = float(r_vals[peak_idx])
    peak_p = float(p_vals[peak_idx]) if np.isfinite(p_vals[peak_idx]) else np.nan
    peak_n = int(n_pairs[peak_idx])

# ---- MAP<65 clustering on rising vs falling temperature ----
# Align Temp to MAP times (no lag) for local slope classification.
idx_m, idx_t, dmins0, temp_at_map = _nn_align(map_times, temp_times, temp_vals, max_abs_minutes=10.0)
if len(idx_m) > 0:
    map_t0 = map_times[idx_m]
    map_v0 = map_series[idx_m]
    temp_t0 = temp_at_map  # already aligned temp values
    # local slope around each MAP time (uses all temp points)
    slopes, slope_ns = _temp_slope_at_map_times(map_t0, temp_times, temp_vals, window_minutes=20.0)
    hypot = map_v0 < 65.0

    rising = np.isfinite(slopes) & (slopes > 0)
    falling = np.isfinite(slopes) & (slopes < 0)

    n_hypot = int(np.sum(hypot))
    n_hypot_rising = int(np.sum(hypot & rising))
    n_hypot_falling = int(np.sum(hypot & falling))
